查看一下我們目前 Rclone 的安裝方式 已知Homebrew的rclone會不支持mount [Image #2] 看看Ubuntu/MacOS等有沒有需要更改安裝方式的部分

```
# Download the official rclone binary into ~/.local/bin (no sudo). Use this when
# the system rclone is too old (apt) or can't mount (Homebrew on macOS). Needs
# curl + unzip; FUSE (macFUSE / fuse3) is still installed separately.
[group('remote-mount')]
rclone-install:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    command -v curl  >/dev/null || { echo "need curl";  exit 1; }
    command -v unzip >/dev/null || { echo "need unzip (brew install unzip / apt install unzip)"; exit 1; }
    case "{{os()}}" in macos) ros=osx ;; *) ros=linux ;; esac
    case "$(uname -m)" in
      x86_64|amd64)  rarch=amd64 ;;
      arm64|aarch64) rarch=arm64 ;;
      *) echo "unsupported arch: $(uname -m)"; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    url="https://downloads.rclone.org/rclone-current-${ros}-${rarch}.zip"
    dest="$HOME/.local/bin"; mkdir -p "$dest"
    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
    echo "downloading $url"
    curl -fSL "$url" -o "$tmp/rclone.zip"
    unzip -q -o "$tmp/rclone.zip" -d "$tmp"
    bin="$(find "$tmp" -type f -name rclone | head -1)"
    [ -n "$bin" ] || { echo "rclone binary not found in archive"; exit 1; }
    install -m 0755 "$bin" "$dest/rclone"
    echo "installed -> $dest/rclone  ($("$dest/rclone" version | head -1))"
    case ":$PATH:" in
      *":$dest:"*) ;;
      *) echo "WARNING: $dest is not on PATH — add to your shell rc:"; echo "  export PATH=\"$dest:\$PATH\"" ;;
    esac
    active="$(command -v rclone 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ "$active" != "$dest/rclone" ]; then
      echo "NOTE: 'rclone' currently resolves to ${active:-none};"
      echo "      ensure $dest precedes it on PATH so the official build wins."
    fi
```

Client-side &#96;mount.ceph&#96; / &#96;slurm-client&#96; / &#96;sssd&#96; are sometimes relevant on a user workstation but only in org-specific setups, so they don't belong in the default install path.\n\nResult: write structured reference docs under a new &#96;docs/infra/&#96; folder. Add cross-links from the existing tools docs and README.\n\n## Deliverables\n\n### New folder: &#96;docs/infra/&#96;\n\nFive new markdown files plus an index README. Each doc is a self-contained reference (~200-400 lines) with:\n\n- Landscape table (tool / license / scope / target user)\n- Decision matrix (\"use X when ...\")\n- Minimal install / quickstart commands (for reference, not auto-run)\n- Links to upstream docs\n- Cross-refs to related docs in this repo\n\n#### 1. &#96;docs/infra/README.md&#96; — Index / decision tree\n\nLanding page with a single mermaid decision tree (\"I want to run a VM\" → laptop? server? cluster?) that routes users to the right sub-doc. Includes a \"what this repo installs vs what's just documented\" boundary statement so future readers don't assume they'll get Proxmox via &#96;chezmoi apply&#96;.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    start[\"I need to run compute / store data somewhere\"] --\u003e q1{Scale?}\n    q1 --\u003e|One VM on my laptop| laptop[virtualization.md#desktop-vm-managers]\n    q1 --\u003e|A few servers / home lab| hypervisor[virtualization.md#bare-metal-hypervisors]\n    q1 --\u003e|Multi-user cluster| cluster{What problem?}\n    cluster --\u003e|Shared files| storage[shared-storage.md]\n    cluster --\u003e|Scheduling jobs| sched[compute-scheduling.md]\n    cluster --\u003e|Single login everywhere| identity[shared-home-identity.md]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 2. &#96;docs/infra/virtualization.md&#96;\n\nCovers three tiers on one page since they're often confused:\n\n- **Desktop VM managers** (per-user, on your laptop): [OrbStack](https://orbstack.dev) (macOS, repo default), [UTM](https://mac.getutm.app) (macOS/QEMU frontend), [VirtualBox](https://www.virtualbox.org) (cross-platform, Oracle), [VMware Fusion](https://www.vmware.com/products/fusion.html) (macOS; now free for personal use), [Parallels Desktop](https://www.parallels.com/) (macOS, commercial), [Lima](https://lima-vm.io) (macOS, headless Linux VMs), [libvirt + virt-manager](https://virt-manager.org) (Linux).\n- **Type-1 bare-metal hypervisors** (installed as host OS): [Proxmox VE](https://www.proxmox.com/en/) (Debian + KVM + LXC, open-source, web UI), [VMware ESXi](https://www.vmware.com/products/esxi-and-esx.html) (commercial, enterprise), [XCP-ng](https://xcp-ng.org) (Citrix Hypervisor fork, open-source), [Harvester](https://harvesterhci.io) (SUSE, K8s-native), [Nutanix CE](https://www.nutanix.com/products/community-edition) (HCI).\n- **Cloud-native VM platforms** (VMs on top of Kubernetes): [KubeVirt](https://kubevirt.io) — note it's orthogonal, used when you already run K8s and want VMs alongside pods.\n\nDecision matrix:\n\n- \"Run one Ubuntu VM on my MacBook\" → OrbStack (already installed) or UTM\n- \"Run 3 VMs with a GUI for a home lab on an old PC\" → Proxmox VE (free, open, web UI, clustering)\n- \"Enterprise vSphere/vCenter ecosystem, commercial support\" → VMware ESXi + vCenter\n- \"Open-source alternative to ESXi, Xen-based\" → XCP-ng + Xen Orchestra\n- \"I already run Kubernetes and want VMs in the same cluster\" → KubeVirt / Harvester\n\nExplicit &#96;OrbStack vs Proxmox&#96; comparison (what the user asked): they don't compete — OrbStack is a macOS app, Proxmox is a server OS. Use OrbStack on your laptop; use Proxmox on a spare physical machine / home lab / colo server.\n\n#### 3. &#96;docs/infra/shared-storage.md&#96;\n\nCluster filesystems comparison (for the \"CephFS?\" question):\n\n- [CephFS](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/cephfs/) — POSIX-compliant distributed FS on top of Ceph RADOS; best when you also want object (RGW) + block (RBD) from the same cluster; heavy to operate (MON/MGR/OSD/MDS daemons).\n- [BeeGFS](https://www.beegfs.io) — parallel FS designed for HPC; high metadata throughput, user-space friendly; dominant in scientific computing clusters; the user explicitly mentioned it for shared home dirs.\n- [Lustre](https://www.lustre.org) — HPC grandaddy; extreme bandwidth, kernel-module client, operational complexity.\n- [GlusterFS](https://www.gluster.org) — simpler \"scale-out NAS\"; FUSE or native client; RedHat abandoning upstream, viability concern.\n- [MooseFS / LizardFS / SeaweedFS / JuiceFS](https://juicefs.com) — lightweight alternatives for smaller teams.\n- [NFSv4 + NFS-Ganesha](https://nfs-ganesha.github.io) — classic shared mount, simplest; single-server bottleneck unless paired with something below.\n- [SMB/CIFS (Samba)](https://www.samba.org) — Windows-interop; fine for mixed desktops.\n- **Cloud-storage clients on Linux**: [rclone](https://rclone.org) (already installed per [README.md](README.md) line 177), [JuiceFS](https://juicefs.com/), [s3fs-fuse](https://github.com/s3fs-fuse/s3fs-fuse).\n\nDecision matrix:\n\n- \"Shared &#96;/home&#96; for 5-20 users on one internal network\" → NFSv4 (simplest) or BeeGFS (if HPC/throughput)\n- \"Ceph-backed K8s + need POSIX FS too\" → CephFS (reuse existing cluster)\n- \"Pure HPC, MPI workloads, thousands of nodes\" → Lustre or BeeGFS\n- \"Windows/Mac desktops mixed in\" → Samba\n- \"Just want S3-like object store\" → MinIO / SeaweedFS / Ceph RGW\n\nClient-side mount recipes (one paragraph each): &#96;mount -t nfs&#96;, &#96;mount -t ceph&#96;, BeeGFS client kernel module, &#96;autofs&#96; for on-demand home mounts.\n\nCross-ref to [docs/tools/containers.md](docs/tools/containers.md) — because shared storage often backs container volumes (CSI drivers).\n\n#### 4. &#96;docs/infra/compute-scheduling.md&#96;\n\nMulti-user auto-allocation of VM/GPU/CPU — the user asked for this specifically:\n\n- [SLURM](https://slurm.schedmd.com) — HPC scheduler; submit batch jobs with &#96;sbatch&#96;, partitioned by QOS/account; gold standard for GPU queues in research labs.\n- [Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io) — general-purpose orchestrator for containers; multi-tenancy via namespaces + ResourceQuotas + LimitRanges; GPU via NVIDIA device plugin; fair-share via [Kueue](https://kueue.sigs.k8s.io) or [Volcano](https://volcano.sh).\n- [Nomad](https://www.nomadproject.io) — HashiCorp scheduler; simpler than K8s, supports containers + raw exec + VMs; pairs well with Terraform/Vault.\n- [HTCondor](https://htcondor.org) / [OpenPBS](https://www.openpbs.org) / [Open Grid Engine](http://gridscheduler.sourceforge.net) — older batch schedulers, still common in some HPC sites.\n- [YARN](https://hadoop.apache.org/docs/stable/hadoop-yarn/hadoop-yarn-site/YARN.html) — Hadoop-era scheduler; relevant only if you're on the Hadoop/Spark-on-YARN stack.\n- [Apache Mesos](https://mesos.apache.org) — historically relevant, largely superseded by K8s.\n- [Ray](https://www.ray.io) / [Dask](https://www.dask.org) — application-level distributed compute, not cluster schedulers per se, but often fill the same role for Python/ML.\n- VM-layer scheduling: [Proxmox cluster with HA](https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/High_Availability) does VM placement; [OpenStack Nova](https://docs.openstack.org/nova/latest/) is the classic IaaS scheduler.\n\nDecision matrix:\n\n- \"ML/HPC research lab, batch GPU jobs, 10-100 users\" → SLURM + shared FS (BeeGFS/Lustre) + FreeIPA\n- \"Modern containerized workloads, multi-tenant product\" → Kubernetes + Kueue/Volcano + namespaces\n- \"Small team, mixed workloads, want simplicity\" → Nomad\n- \"VM placement in a Proxmox cluster\" → built-in Proxmox HA + affinity rules\n- \"Spark/Hive jobs on legacy Hadoop\" → YARN\n\n#### 5. &#96;docs/infra/shared-home-identity.md&#96;\n\nThe user explicitly asked about \"大家 user home dir 都管理在同一個 NAS server (e.g. BeeGFS)\". This is two problems solved together:\n\n- **Shared storage layer**: NFSv4 / BeeGFS / CephFS exports &#96;/home&#96;, all nodes mount it. Typically via &#96;autofs&#96; for per-user lazy mount.\n- **Identity layer**: UIDs/GIDs must match across all nodes, otherwise file permissions break. Solved with LDAP-style central directory:\n  - [FreeIPA](https://www.freeipa.org) — RedHat's integrated stack (389ds LDAP + MIT Kerberos + DNS + Dogtag PKI + web UI); easiest turnkey for Linux fleets\n  - [389 Directory Server](https://directory.fedoraproject.org/) — the standalone LDAP piece\n  - [OpenLDAP](https://www.openldap.org) — classic, more manual\n  - [Samba AD DC](https://wiki.samba.org/index.php/Setting_up_Samba_as_an_Active_Directory_Domain_Controller) — if you need Windows-compatible AD\n  - Cloud identity: [JumpCloud](https://jumpcloud.com), [Okta](https://www.okta.com), [Azure AD / Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/whatis)\n- **Client integration**: [SSSD](https://sssd.io) caches directory lookups + resolves UIDs + mounts home-on-login via &#96;pam_mkhomedir&#96; / &#96;pam_exec&#96;. On macOS, the corresponding binding uses &#96;dsconfigldap&#96; or MDM.\n\nReference architecture diagram (mermaid):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    user[User login] --\u003e sshd[sshd / login PAM]\n    sshd --\u003e sssd[SSSD]\n    sssd --\u003e|LDAP| ipa[FreeIPA / 389ds]\n    sssd --\u003e|Kerberos| ipa\n    sshd --\u003e|pam_mount / autofs| nfs[NFS / BeeGFS server]\n    nfs --\u003e home[\"/home/\u0026lt;user\u0026gt;\"]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nInclude GID/UID-range conventions (reserve \u003e= 10000 for directory users, \u003c 1000 for system), and a note that K8s pods must match these UIDs via &#96;securityContext.runAsUser&#96; to write to mounted home volumes.\n\n### Cross-links to update\n\n- [README.md](README.md) line 168 (\"### Tools (via ansible)\") — add a small \"### Reference docs\" subsection just below, pointing to &#96;docs/infra/README.md&#96; (so new readers discover the folder):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;markdown\n### Reference docs (no install)\n\n- **Infrastructure \u0026 virtualization**: [docs/infra/](docs/infra/) — Proxmox / ESXi / OrbStack / UTM comparison; CephFS / BeeGFS / NFS shared storage; SLURM / Kubernetes compute scheduling; FreeIPA + shared-home patterns. Documentation only; nothing is installed by chezmoi for these.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- [docs/tools/containers.md](docs/tools/containers.md) — at the top \"Primary pain points\" paragraph, add a \"See also\" line linking to &#96;docs/infra/virtualization.md#desktop-vm-managers&#96; since OrbStack's VM-manager side lives there, and &#96;docs/infra/shared-storage.md&#96; for when container volumes hit CSI/CephFS.\n\n- [docs/tools/infrastructure-as-code.md](docs/tools/infrastructure-as-code.md) \"Related\" section — add a link to &#96;docs/infra/&#96; since Terraform/OpenTofu + these infra concepts are the same domain (IaC for infra discussed in IaC doc; infra itself discussed here).\n\n## Out of scope (explicitly)\n\n- No chezmoi prompt, no ansible role, no Homebrew formula, no Brewfile entry.\n- No deep tutorial (e.g. \"how to install Proxmox step by step\") — link to upstream docs instead.\n- No Kubernetes cluster bootstrap, no kubectl config management (can be a separate future plan).\n- No &#96;mount.ceph&#96; / &#96;beegfs-client&#96; ansible role (would be org-specific; leave as docs commands).",

98	# All `chezmoi-*` recipes pass `--no-pager` so output streams straight to

100	# Critical for non-interactive callers (CI, coding agents, `just` itself
101	# in scripted contexts) — without it, delta tries to alternate-screen
102	# / line-buffer over a pipe and either panics, hangs, or eats output.

116	# session, etc.). See pitfalls/bootstrap-no-tty-sudo-prompt-skipped.md.
117	# Prompts once, validates against sudo, shreds tmpfile on exit.
118	#     just apply-with-sudo                      # interactive prompt

136	# Run the interactive bootstrap wrapper from the LOCAL chezmoi source.
137	# Use this instead of `curl|bash` when you're on a slow / GFW-throttled network
138	# and have already cloned the repo. Skips the bootstrap.sh stage entirely:
139	# uv resolves PEP 723 deps locally; chezmoi init clones from the same remote
140	# you're cloned from. Pass extra args after `--`:

157	# (the `--prompt` is what re-fires promptXOnce; without it the old values win).

180	# ============================================================================
181	# Dotfiles backup (~/.dotfiles_backup)
182	# ============================================================================
183	#
184	# Pre-apply snapshots produced by `run_before_01_backup_dotfiles.sh.tmpl`.
185	# `backupMode` ∈ {smart (default), full, off}; smart only captures files
186	# `chezmoi apply` would overwrite/delete (per `chezmoi status` col 2 = M/D).
187	
188	# List backup snapshots with file count
189	list-backups:
190	    @if [ ! -d "$HOME/.dotfiles_backup" ]; then echo "No backups in ~/.dotfiles_backup"; exit 0; fi
191	    @for d in "$HOME"/.dotfiles_backup/*/; do \
192	        [ -d "$d" ] || continue; \
193	        ts=$(basename "$d"); \
194	        n=$(find "$d" -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '); \
195	        printf '%s  (%s file(s))\n' "$ts" "$n"; \
196	    done
197	
198	# Diff a backup snapshot against current files in ~ (read-only inspection)
199	diff-backup ts:
200	    @snap="$HOME/.dotfiles_backup/{{ts}}"; \
201	    if [ ! -d "$snap" ]; then echo "No such backup: {{ts}}" >&2; exit 1; fi; \
202	    find "$snap" -type f | while read -r backed; do \
203	        rel="${backed#$snap/}"; live="$HOME/$rel"; \
204	        if [ ! -e "$live" ]; then \
205	            printf '\n=== %s: in backup, missing from live ===\n' "$rel"; \
206	        elif ! cmp -s "$backed" "$live"; then \
207	            printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$rel"; \
208	            diff -u "$backed" "$live" || true; \
209	        fi; \
210	    done

519	fleet-apply *ARGS:
520	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py {{ARGS}}
521	
522	# Edit fleet inventory (~/.config/fleet/machines.toml). Seeds an empty
523	# template on first run; opens with $EDITOR (defaults to nvim).
524	fleet-edit:
525	    @mkdir -p ~/.config/fleet
526	    @if [ ! -f ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml ]; then \
527	        echo "[INFO] seeding empty ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — add [[hosts]] entries below"; \
528	        printf '# fleet-apply inventory — see docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md\n# Schema reference: dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl\n\n[defaults]\nchezmoi_path    = "auto"\nconnect_timeout = 30\ncommand_timeout = 7200\n\n# [[hosts]]\n# name      = "lab-box"\n# ssh_alias = "lab-box"\n# no_root_machine = false\n# password_source = { type = "prompt" }\n' > ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml; \
529	        chmod 600 ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml; \
530	    fi
531	    "${EDITOR:-nvim}" ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml
532	
533	
534	# Pre-flight readiness probe across all configured hosts. Predicts what
535	# `just fleet-apply` would do per host (up-to-date / behind / drift / busy
536	# / toml-mismatch / not-init / unreachable / ...) WITHOUT changing anything.
537	# Read-only, ~1.5s per host (with `git fetch`). See docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md
538	# § Readiness probe.
539	fleet-status *ARGS:
540	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --readiness {{ARGS}}
541	
542	# Like fleet-status but skip remote `git fetch` (faster, but 'behind' state
543	# may be stale). Useful offline or when you only care about drift / busy.
544	fleet-status-quick *ARGS:
545	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --readiness --readiness-no-fetch {{ARGS}}
546	
547	
548	# Preview only: runs `chezmoi diff` on every host (no changes applied)
549	fleet-apply-dry-run *ARGS:
550	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --dry-run {{ARGS}}
551	
552	# Quick `chezmoi diff` against ONE host (serial, debug-friendly output).
553	# Use this in vibe loops to see exactly what your latest commit will do
554	# on a specific machine before pushing/applying for real.
555	fleet-diff HOST *ARGS:
556	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --dry-run --hosts {{HOST}} --serial {{ARGS}}
557	
558	# Apply ONLY a single chezmoi target on each host (skips ansible / Brewfile).
559	# PATH is the chezmoi target path, e.g. `.config/zsh/aliases.zsh` or
560	# `.zshrc`. Fast feedback for editing one dotfile across the fleet without
561	# waiting for full Linuxbrew/ansible cycles. Pass extra `--hosts HOST` to
562	# scope. Internally sets CHEZMOI_FLEET_APPLY_PATH so the wrapper runs
563	# `chezmoi apply <relpath>` instead of `chezmoi update --init`.
564	fleet-apply-file PATH *ARGS:
565	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --apply-only-path {{PATH}} {{ARGS}}
566	
567	# Apply a feature BRANCH instead of pulling main. Each remote does
568	# `git fetch origin BRANCH && git checkout -B BRANCH origin/BRANCH &&
569	# git merge --ff-only origin/BRANCH` before chezmoi apply. Fails loud
570	# on divergence — use `just fleet-apply-branch-force` to nuke local
571	# state with `git reset --hard`. Local hosts skip this entirely (source
572	# is your editor's working tree).
573	fleet-apply-branch BRANCH *ARGS:
574	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --branch {{BRANCH}} {{ARGS}}
575	
576	# Like fleet-apply-branch but uses `git reset --hard origin/BRANCH` on
577	# remotes, destroying any local divergence. Use after force-pushing a
578	# rebased topic branch so every host follows.
579	fleet-apply-branch-force BRANCH *ARGS:
580	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --branch {{BRANCH}} --force-checkout {{ARGS}}
581	
582	# Apply to a single named host in --serial mode (debug-friendly output)
583	fleet-apply-one HOST *ARGS:
584	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --hosts {{HOST}} --serial {{ARGS}}
585	
586	# Kill orphan chezmoi/ansible processes on every host (cleanup after Ctrl+C)
587	fleet-apply-kill *ARGS:
588	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --kill-orphans {{ARGS}}
589	
590	# Probe each host for running chezmoi/ansible (use after killing local SSH)
591	fleet-apply-status *ARGS:
592	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --status {{ARGS}}
593	
594	# Like fleet-apply-status but re-poll every Ns until everyone is idle
595	# (Ctrl+C to stop). Default interval 10s; override with --watch=N in ARGS.
596	fleet-apply-watch *ARGS:
597	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --status --watch 10 {{ARGS}}

599	# Live-tail the remote fleet-apply log of HOST (defaults to most recent run);
600	# pass `HOST:RUN_ID` (e.g. lab-box:20260422T133615Z) to pin a specific run.
601	# Ctrl+C stops the viewer only — the remote run keeps going.

1	# dotfiles
2	
3	Cross-platform development environment setup using **chezmoi** + **ansible**.
4	
5	- **chezmoi**: manages config files (dotfiles)
6	- **ansible**: installs system dependencies and tools
7	
8	## Prerequisites
9	
10	- [chezmoi](https://www.chezmoi.io/install/)
11	- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (for ansible)
12	
13	## Architecture
14	
15	```mermaid
16	flowchart TB
17	    subgraph Bootstrap["1. Bootstrap"]
18	        BREW[Homebrew macOS]
19	        UV[uv] --> ANS[ansible]
20	        MISE[mise]
21	    end
22	
23	    subgraph Chezmoi["2. chezmoi apply"]
24	        DOT[Config files<br/>~/.gitconfig, ~/.config/]
25	        ANSDIR[~/.ansible/]
26	        BREWFILE[Brewfiles<br/>~/.config/homebrew/]
27	    end
28	
29	    subgraph Ansible["3. Ansible Playbooks"]
30	        BASE[base]
31	        ZSH[zsh]
32	        NVIM[neovim]
33	        DEVTOOLS[devtools]
34	        UVTOOLS[python_uv_tools]
35	        CARGO[rust_cargo_tools]
36	        LLMTOOLS[llm_tools]
37	    end
38	
39	    subgraph BrewBundle["4. Brew Bundle opt-in"]
40	        CASKS[GUI Apps]
41	        MAS[App Store]
42	    end
43	
44	    Bootstrap --> Chezmoi --> Ansible
45	    Chezmoi -.-> BrewBundle
46	    MISE -.->|Node.js, Rust| NVIM
47	    MISE -.->|Rust| CARGO
48	    UV -.->|Python tools| UVTOOLS
49	    UV -.->|LiteLLM| LLMTOOLS

51	    BREW -.->|formulae / casks| LLMTOOLS
52	```
53	
54	## Quick Setup
55	
56	### Interactive (recommended)
57	
58	```bash
59	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash
60	```
61	
62	Installs [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (if missing) and launches `dotfiles-init` — a Python wrapper that groups the ~19 chezmoi prompts into a clean multi-select UI, offers pre-set bundles (`personal-mac` / `work-mac` / `server-linux` / `cloud-vm` / `minimal`), checks SSH keys, then calls real `chezmoi init` with your answers pre-filled. Full docs: [`scripts/init/README.md`](scripts/init/README.md).
63	
64	On first-run or slow networks the `uv` resolver can sit silently for a few minutes — use the verbose form to see timestamped progress + `uv --verbose` resolver output + `set -x`:
65	
66	```bash
67	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | DOTFILES_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE=1 bash
68	```
69	
70	Pass extra args through to the wrapper via `bash -s --` (e.g. run the schema-parity checker instead of the default `init`):
71	
72	```bash
73	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/main/bootstrap.sh | bash -s -- doctor
74	```
75	
76	Behind GFW? Set `DOTFILES_RAW_URL` / `DOTFILES_REF` to point at a mirror, or use the non-interactive path below.
77	
78	### Non-interactive (direct chezmoi)
79	
80	```bash
81	# Installs chezmoi to ~/.local/bin and walks through the raw prompts one-by-one.
82	# Uses HTTPS to avoid SSH key setup on fresh machines.
83	export GITHUB_USERNAME=daviddwlee84
84	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin" init --apply "https://github.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git"
85	
86	# After install, switch the chezmoi source repo to SSH (so future `chezmoi update` uses your SSH key):
87	#   chezmoi cd
88	#   git remote set-url origin git@github.com:$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git
89	#   exit
90	```
91	
92	This automatically:
93	
94	1. Bootstraps Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, mise, ansible
95	2. Deploys all config files
96	3. Runs ansible playbooks (git, ripgrep, fd, neovim, etc.)
97	4. Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` is enabled, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps` is enabled)
98	
99	#### Sudo password injection (when chezmoi can't open `/dev/tty`)
100	
101	Some Linux environments — notably **CentOS 7 + AD/LDAP user with high UID** where `pam_systemd` never created `/run/user/<UID>/` — leave the chezmoi-spawned bootstrap script unable to open `/dev/tty`, so the shared sudo helper can't prompt and Linuxbrew aborts with `Insufficient permissions to install Homebrew to "/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew"`. The fix is to pre-stage the password via `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (the same env-var [`fleet_apply`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md) uses over SSH).
102	
103	The repo ships [`scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh`](scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh) to handle the prompt → 0600 tmpfile → export → run → `shred` dance:
104	
105	```bash
106	# First time (chezmoi not installed yet):
107	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin"   # install chezmoi only
108	bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles/main/scripts/apply_with_sudo.sh) \
109	  --init "https://github.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git"
110	
111	# Re-runs (after chezmoi source is cloned at ~/.local/share/chezmoi):
112	just apply-with-sudo                                              # interactive prompt
113	just apply-with-sudo --pass-from-env                              # reads $SUDO_PASSWORD
114	SUDO_PASSWORD=xxx just apply-with-sudo --pass-from-env            # one-liner
115	```
116	
117	The wrapper validates the password against `sudo -v` before invoking `chezmoi`, then shreds the tmpfile on exit (any signal). Inside chezmoi's run-scripts, `sudo_session_init` adopts the file, moves it into the shared state dir, and spawns the watchdog that keeps the sudo timestamp warm.
118	
119	**Even simpler alternative** if you have root and don't mind editing sudoers: add `$USER ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL` to `/etc/sudoers.d/99-bootstrap`, run `chezmoi apply`, then remove the line. The shared helper short-circuits cleanly when sudo is truly passwordless.
120	
121	> CentOS 7 also blocks Linuxbrew install because system curl 7.29 is older than Homebrew's 7.41 minimum, and Homebrew bottles built on Ubuntu 22.04+ don't run on glibc 2.17 anyway. Linuxbrew is fully optional on Linux — every ansible task that uses it has a non-brew fallback (cargo / GitHub musl release / AppImage). On CentOS 7, drop a stub `~/.local/bin/brew` (`#!/bin/sh\nexit 0`) before applying to short-circuit the bootstrap's brew step.
122	
123	Full diagnosis: [`pitfalls/bootstrap-no-tty-sudo-prompt-skipped.md`](pitfalls/bootstrap-no-tty-sudo-prompt-skipped.md) and [`pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md`](pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md).
124	
125	### After install
126	
127	- `~/.local/bin` and the rest of the shared layer (mise/uv/cargo/bun PATH, plus Linux OpenCode's `~/.opencode/bin`) are exported via `~/.config/shell/00_exports.sh`, sourced by both the chezmoi-managed `~/.bashrc` and `~/.zshrc`.
128	- On sudo-enabled machines, the ansible role for your `primaryShell` choice switches your login shell automatically (`zsh` role for `primaryShell=zsh`, `bash` role for `primaryShell=bash`). Log out / back in to pick it up, or run `exec zsh` / `exec bash` now.
129	- `primaryShell=bash` on macOS additionally installs Homebrew bash 5.x and adds it to `/etc/shells` (system bash 3.2 is too old for oh-my-bash plugins + ble.sh). zsh-primary mac users see no extra brew install.
130	- On `noRoot=true` installs, login shell isn't changed — run `exec zsh` / `exec bash` per session, or ask your sysadmin: `sudo chsh -s "$(command -v zsh)" $USER` (or `bash`).
131	- Open a new shell after install so PATH changes take effect. Both `~/.bashrc` and `~/.zshrc` are deployed regardless of `primaryShell` choice, so the other shell still works ad-hoc.
132	
133	### Optional Components
134	
135	During `chezmoi init`, you'll be prompted for optional installs. The prompts
136	themselves are defined once in [`scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`](scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py)
137	(`PROMPTS`) and generated into `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `Dockerfile`; this table
138	is coverage-checked against that list by `dotfiles_init.py gen --check`.
139	
140	<!-- dotfiles-init:prompts (coverage-checked by scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py gen --check) -->
141	| Option | Default | Description |
142	|--------|---------|-------------|
143	| `installCodingAgents` | true | Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI (`agy`), RTK, td, sidecar, specify-cli, etc. |
144	| `installBitwarden` | false | Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) + Desktop app (desktop profiles) with SSH agent auto-detection |
145	| `installPythonUvTools` | true | Python CLI tools via uv (mlflow, sqlit-tui, tmuxp, etc.) |
146	| `installJsCliTools` | true | Standalone JS/npm CLI utilities (readability-cli for terminal web reader, etc.) |
147	| `installLlmTools` | false | Local LLM tools: Ollama, LiteLLM, llmfit, models |
148	| `installAiDesktopApps` | false | macOS AI desktop apps via Homebrew Brewfile (Claude, ChatGPT, OpenCode Desktop, Antigravity, Codex Desktop on Apple Silicon; `ollama-app` also requires `installLlmTools=true`). macOS only. |
149	| `installBrewApps` | false | General GUI apps via Homebrew Brewfile (terminals, browsers, utilities, mas; excludes AI desktop apps). Desktop profiles only (`macos`/`ubuntu_desktop`). |
150	| `installInputMethod` | false | Traditional Chinese input methods (McBopomofo, RIME/Squirrel on macOS; ibus-rime on Linux). Desktop profiles only (`macos`/`ubuntu_desktop`). |
151	| `discordChannel` | `flatpak` | Discord install channel on `ubuntu_desktop`: `flatpak` (recommended), `deb`, or `none`. macOS uses the Brewfile cask; servers skip. |
152	| `installNiri` | false | [niri](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri) scrollable-tiling Wayland compositor, built from source (`ubuntu_desktop` only). Installs the binary + GDM session/systemd files; NVIDIA gets a VRAM application-profile automatically. See [docs/playbooks/niri.md](docs/playbooks/niri.md). |
153	| `installNetworkingTools` | false | Networking CLI tools (nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy, bandwhich, rustscan, etc.) |
154	| `installTunnelTools` | false | Tunnel tools (ngrok, cloudflared) — expose localhost / SSH reverse tunnels |
155	| `installIacTools` | false | Infrastructure-as-Code CLIs (Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu) |
156	| `installMediaTools` | false | Media/AV CLI tools ([ffmpeg](docs/tools/ffmpeg.md), [ImageMagick](docs/tools/imagemagick.md), [exiftool](docs/tools/exiftool.md), [libvips](docs/tools/libvips.md)). Also satisfies vhs's runtime ffmpeg dep. |
157	| `installDotnetTools` | false | .NET SDK via mise + dotnet global tools ([azure-cost-cli](docs/tools/dotnet-tools.md) for Azure cost analysis) |
158	| `installExtraRuntimes` | true | Extra mise runtimes (rust, bun, ruby; ~1.8GB) + their cargo/gem tool roles. Node is always installed regardless. Set false for lean cloud VMs / CI. |
159	| `installAuditd` | false | Linux audit framework (auditd) + baseline rules (identity / sudoers / sshd_config / privileged-exec). Linux only. See [docs/sysadmin/auditd.md](docs/sysadmin/auditd.md). |
160	| `installHomelabTools` | false | Homelab hardware-monitoring CLIs (lm-sensors, smartmontools, ipmitool, nvme-cli, storcli) + `hw-*` shell helpers, each gated on detected hardware. Linux only; no-op in VMs. See [docs/sysadmin/hardware.md](docs/sysadmin/hardware.md). |
161	| `useChineseMirror` | false | Switch Homebrew / pip / npm / cargo / etc. to China (GFW) mirrors |
162	| `gitleaksAllRepos` | false | Run gitleaks on ALL git repos, not just those with `.pre-commit-config.yaml` |
163	| `backupMode` | `smart` | Back up existing dotfiles before apply: `smart` (only files chezmoi overwrites), `full` (fixed allowlist), `off` (skip) |
164	| `allowPartialFailure` | false | Continue installing other Ansible roles if one role fails |
165	| `noRoot` | false | Skip sudo-requiring tasks (for servers without root access). Linux only. |
166	| `motdStyle` | `figlet` | SSH login banner style: `figlet` (~6 lines, default), `fastfetch-slim` (figlet + fastfetch w/o logo, ~10 lines), `fastfetch-full` (full distro logo + everything, ~22 lines). Runtime override: `MOTD_STYLE=...` in `~/.zshrc.adhoc`. See [docs/zsh/motd.md](docs/zsh/motd.md). |
167	| `primaryShell` | `zsh` | Primary interactive shell: `zsh` (default, full-featured) or `bash` (oh-my-bash + ble.sh, close-to-zsh UX). Both `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc` deploy on every host; this only governs which shell `chsh` switches to as the login shell. See [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md) for the bash side's known gaps and tradeoffs. |
168	| `enableVimMode` | true | Vim-style modal editing in shells (zsh-vi-mode, `set -o vi`, ble.sh) + tmux vim navigation. Does NOT affect Neovim. See [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md). |
169	<!-- /dotfiles-init:prompts -->
170	
171	To change options later, don't hand-edit `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` — run the reconfigure tool, which seeds the same TUI from your current values and re-applies via `chezmoi init --apply --prompt`:
172	
173	```bash
174	just reconfigure                 # interactive (or: czcfg)
175	just reconfigure -- --set installLlmTools=true --yes   # non-interactive single key
176	```
177	
178	See [`scripts/init/README.md`](scripts/init/README.md) → "Reconfigure".
179	
180	## What You Get
181	
182	### Config Files
183	
184	- `~/.gitconfig` - Git configuration; managed via `modify_` so `gh auth setup-git`'s `[credential "..."]` blocks (with the per-machine absolute path to `gh`) survive `chezmoi apply` ([docs](docs/tools/gh-cli.md))
185	- `~/.config/git/hooks/` - Global Git hooks (pre-commit + Git LFS hooks)
186	- `~/.config/gh-dash/config.yml` - Global gh-dash config, with `diffnav` as the diff pager
187	- `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml` - Global LazyGit config, with `delta` as the custom diff pager
188	- `~/.config/bat/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme` - Managed Tokyo Night theme for bat; apply rebuilds the bat cache and clears it if the cache is incompatible with `delta`
189	- `~/.config/nvim/` - Neovim (LazyVim) configuration; system clipboard via `unnamedplus`, with an SSH-conditional OSC 52 override so remote yanks reach the local clipboard (pairs with tmux `set-clipboard on`, see [docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md#osc-52-clipboard-ssh-friendly-yank))
190	- `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` - uv package manager config (PyPI: official / Aliyun+TUNA+USTC via `useChineseMirror`)
191	- `~/.cargo/config.toml` - Cargo registry config (crates.io / TUNA sparse index via `useChineseMirror`)
192	- `~/.npmrc` - npm registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
193	- `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` - Bun global registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
194	- `~/.gemrc` - RubyGems source + common options (TUNA mirror; only managed when `useChineseMirror=true`, gated via `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`)
195	- `~/.condarc` - Conda/Mamba channels with TUNA Anaconda mirror (only managed when `useChineseMirror=true`, preserves `auto_activate_base`/user channel prefs)
196	- `~/.config/zsh/00_exports.zsh` - Env-var mirror bundle (Homebrew / Rustup / mise / GOPROXY) when `useChineseMirror=true`; also exported by bootstrap + ansible runner scripts so first-run installs and ansible subprocesses inherit them ([docs](docs/tools/mirrors.md))
197	- `~/.config/zsh/99_local_proxy.zsh` - Create-only machine-local proxy override stub; uncomment `LOCAL_PROXY_URL` / `LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` here to pin Clash ports without future chezmoi diffs
198	- `~/.docker/config.json` - Docker client `proxies.default` block (auto-injected from `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` / `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL`; preserves `auths` / `credsStore` via chezmoi modify-script) ([docs](docs/tools/containers.md))
199	- `~/.config/docker/daemon.json` - Rootless Docker `registry-mirrors` (DaoCloud / USTC / NJU / ...; Linux + `useChineseMirror` only) ([docs](docs/tools/containers.md#strategy-a-registry-mirrors-in-daemonjson))
200	- `~/.config/alacritty/` - Alacritty terminal config (CSI-u keybindings for `Ctrl+Number` tmux window switching, `option_as_alt` for Meta keys)
201	- `~/Library/Application Support/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/User/` (macOS) + `~/.config/{Code,Cursor,Antigravity}/User/` (Linux) - Editor settings overlay: `modify_settings.json` deep-merges a 6-key baseline (Hack Nerd Font Mono, relative line numbers, format on save, smart-accept suggestion, terminal font) into each editor's live `settings.json` without overwriting other keys; `create_keybindings.json` seeds 5 universal keybindings on a fresh machine and never overwrites editor-added entries. Canonical templates live under [`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`](.chezmoitemplates/editor/); `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` gates each editor dir with a `stat` presence check so uninstalled editors never produce phantom directories.
202	- `~/.config/ghostty/config` - Ghostty/cmux terminal config (`macos-option-as-alt` for tmux Meta keybindings, disabled ligatures, explicit `clipboard-write = allow` / `clipboard-read = ask` for OSC 52) ([docs](docs/tools/ghostty.md))
203	- `~/.config/starship.toml` - Starship cross-shell prompt config
204	- `~/.xonshrc` + `~/.config/xonsh/rc.xsh` - Optional [Xonsh](https://xon.sh/) (Python-superset shell) startup + extension sandbox. Installed via `python_uv_tools` with a curated set of xontribs (`jedi`/`zoxide`/`pipeliner`/`fzf-widgets`); **not** a login shell — drop in with `xonsh` for ad-hoc Python-in-shell work ([docs](docs/shells/xonsh.md))
205	- `~/.config/direnv/direnvrc` - direnv helper functions, including `.venv`-aware Python activation
206	- `~/.config/yazi/` - Yazi file manager config (v0.3.3+ syntax, [docs](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/overview/))
207	  - `yazi.toml` - Main config with open rules and openers (`o`/`O`)
208	  - `keymap.toml`, `theme.toml` - Optional customization files (stubs provided)
209	- `~/.config/btop/btop.conf` + `~/.config/btop/themes/catppuccin_mocha.theme` - btop system-monitor baseline (Catppuccin Mocha theme, process tree view, `vim_keys` mirrors `enableVimMode`); seeded once via `create_` so btop's on-exit config rewrites never cause chezmoi drift; catppuccin theme vendored like bat's ([docs](docs/tools/btop.md))
210	- `~/.claude/` - Claude Code settings
211	- `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml` - Coding-agent CLI overlays: each `modify_*` script deep-merges a small managed baseline (preferences, features, curated plugins) into the CLI's live config, preserving auth tokens, per-project trust, sessions, and other machine-local state. Codex specifically round-trips `[projects]` and `[marketplaces.*]` so per-project trust paths never get clobbered. OpenCode legacy `~/.config/opencode/config.json` is migrated to the modern filename by a one-shot `run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`. Full design: [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
212	- `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` - Global SpecStory defaults for `specstory run` across all projects
213	- `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins (resurrect, continuum, tmux-floax floating pane, tmux-fzf for fuzzy keybinding/session/pane search rebound to `prefix+?`, tmux-fzf-url, tmux-open), vim-style copy mode with clipboard yank, capture-pane helpers (`prefix+y`/`Y`/`C-y`), a native popup menu (`prefix+Space` or `prefix+e`, script-driven with submenus and height-aware trimming) with layout/resize/session management, popup shell (`prefix+\``) and lazygit popup (`prefix+G`), a glow-rendered cheatsheet (`prefix+Space` → `?`), vim-style pane nav, `Ctrl+1..9` quick window switching (CSI-u terminals), extended-keys for coding agents (including `Ctrl+/` in Neovim), sesh keybindings (`prefix+g` fzf picker, `prefix+T` television picker, `prefix+O` built-in picker, `prefix+W` window picker, `prefix+S` last), responsive Catppuccin status bar (adapts modules to terminal width for mobile), and config reload on `prefix+R` ([docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md))
214	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` - Cross-platform terminal wrapper for `copy` / `copy-file` / `paste` / `open`; `x copy` has an OSC 52 fallback for SSH text copy, while `x copy-file` copies desktop file objects for Finder / Files paste ([docs](docs/tools/clipboard.md))
215	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/sms` - Huawei router SMS reader (HiLink XML API; verification-code extraction, clipboard integration, TV channel) ([docs](docs/tools/sms.md))
216	- `~/.config/sms/config.toml.example` - Starter config for the `sms` CLI (real `config.toml` is created at runtime, never committed)

230	- `~/.config/television/cable/skills.toml` + `~/.config/television/cable/skills-walk.toml` - Two Television channels for browsing agent skills: `skills` parses `npx skills list` (project + global, with Agents column), `skills-walk` walks `~/.agents/`, `~/.claude/`, `~/.codex/`, `~/.cursor/skills-cursor/` directly without invoking npx; both preview SKILL.md with bat
231	- `~/.config/television/cable/agent-sessions.toml` + `~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py` - Unified Television channel for coding-agent sessions across OpenCode (SQLite), Claude Code (JSONL), Codex (JSONL), Cursor Agent CLI (store.db), and Cursor IDE composer chats (state.vscdb); 6 source cycles (all/per-agent), content-searchable via first-user-message snippet, `Enter` prints `cd <dir> && <agent> --resume <id>`, `Alt+T` resumes in current shell (Cursor IDE: opens workspace folder via `cursor <dir>` since IDE has no chat-resume CLI flag)

258	SSH files are managed as create-only templates: if `~/.ssh/config` already exists, it is not overwritten. In that case, add `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` to your existing config manually to load the managed snippets.

260	### Upstream Clones (via `.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`)
261	
262	Vendored upstream sources are declared in [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl) and auto-refreshed weekly by chezmoi (`refreshPeriod = "168h"`). Force an immediate pull with `chezmoi apply --refresh-externals`.

264	- `~/.oh-my-zsh` + 4 custom plugins (`zsh-autosuggestions`, `zsh-syntax-highlighting`, `zsh-completions`, `zsh-vi-mode`*) — *`zsh-vi-mode` is conditional on the `enableVimMode` chezmoi prompt (default `true`); see [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
265	- `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm` (TPM)
266	- `~/.fzf` (Linux only; apt version lacks `--zsh`)
267	- `~/.local/share/toolkami/toolkami.rb`
268	
269	See [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md#companion-file-chezmoiexternalformat) for details and when to add entries here vs. ansible.

316	## Supported Platforms
317	
318	| Platform | Package Manager | Notes |
319	|----------|-----------------|-------|
320	| macOS | Homebrew | Full support |
321	| Ubuntu Desktop | apt + snap | Full support |
322	| Ubuntu Server | apt + snap | Full support |
323	| Ubuntu Server (no root) | GitHub binaries + mise + cargo + uv | `noRoot=true`, tools installed to `~/.local/bin` |
324	| Raspberry Pi 5 (64-bit OS) | apt + Linuxbrew | Full support (same as Ubuntu Server) |
325	| Raspberry Pi 4 (32-bit OS) | apt + GitHub binaries | Linuxbrew skipped; some tools without armhf builds are skipped |

327	## Manual Commands
328	
329	```bash
330	chezmoi diff          # Preview changes
331	chezmoi apply         # Apply config files
332	chezmoi cd            # Go to source directory
333	
334	# Re-run ansible manually
335	cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml
336	```
337	
338	## Keeping tools up-to-date
339	
340	`chezmoi apply` is deliberately **install-only** — ansible roles mostly use
341	`state: present` / `creates:` idempotency so re-applying never silently bumps
342	every tool on your machine. For explicit upgrades, use the dedicated entry
343	points (see [`docs/this_repo/upgrades.md`](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) for the full matrix):
344	
345	```bash
346	just upgrade-all          # externals + brew + mise + uv + npm + cargo + dotnet + gem + agents + plugins
347	just upgrade-dry-run      # preview without executing
348	
349	# Per category (compose as you like):
350	just upgrade-brew         # formulas + casks (--greedy) + Brewfile (no --no-upgrade) + cleanup
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Tool managers — who installs what
2	
3	A map of every tool installed by this repo, organised by the manager that
4	owns it. Companion to [`upgrades.md`](upgrades.md) — that one is the
5	upgrade-side reference; this one is install-side.
6

8

10	|---|---|

13	| "I'm adding a new tool — which manager should I use?" | [§ Decision tree](#decision-tree-for-new-tools) |

15	| "How is X upgraded?" | [`upgrades.md`](upgrades.md) |
16	
17	> Convention reminder: install-only by design (see [`upgrades.md` § Why
18	> install and upgrade are split](upgrades.md#why-install-and-upgrade-are-split)).
19	> Every install path here uses `state: present` / `creates:` / `[[ -d … ]]`
20	> guards; nothing in `chezmoi apply` silently bumps a tool's version. The
21	> only thing that intentionally moves tools forward is

47	
48	## Install order
49	
50	Five phases in chronological order. Anything earlier MUST be present
51	before the next phase can run.
52	
53	```
54	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│ Phase 0 — Bootstrap (run_once_before_*)                                 │
56	│   curl-installer: Homebrew, uv, mise                                    │
57	│   apt: build-essential, git, curl (Linux prereqs for Linuxbrew)         │
58	│   apt: libffi-dev, libyaml-dev, python3-dev (Linux non-noRoot only)     │
59	│   uv: ansible-core (pinned Python 3.13)                                 │
60	│   ansible-galaxy: community.general collection                          │
61	│   mise: install runtimes from ~/.config/mise/config.toml                │
62	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
63	                                  │
64	                                  ▼
65	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
66	│ Phase 1 — chezmoi apply (config file deploy)                            │
67	│   Deploys dot_* files; doesn't install tools directly                   │
68	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
69	                                  │
70	                                  ▼
71	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
72	│ Phase 2 — Ansible (run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles)                 │
73	│   Runs all 26 roles; each dispatches to its underlying manager          │
74	│   (brew / apt / mise / uv / npm / cargo / gem / dotnet / curl / gh-rel) │
75	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
76	                                  │
77	                                  ▼
78	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
79	│ Phase 3 — Brew bundle (run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle)               │
80	│   `brew bundle --no-upgrade` against ~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile*       │
81	│   Mostly GUI casks (macOS); skipped if installBrewApps=false            │
82	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
83	                                  │
84	                                  ▼
85	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
86	│ Phase 4 — Per-application onchange scripts                              │
87	│   Completion regen (run_after_50_generate_completions)                  │
88	│   bat theme cache (run_onchange_after_25_bat_theme)                     │
89	│   ble.sh compile (run_onchange_after_26_install_blesh)                  │
90	│   Global skills restore (run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills)   │
91	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
92	```
93	
94	The bootstrap is **single-source-of-truth** for the foundational tools
95	that everything else depends on. If you find yourself wanting to add
96	`mise` / `uv` / Homebrew elsewhere, the answer is almost always "extend
97	the bootstrap, then assume it in the role". The Linux noRoot path
98	(`profile=ubuntu_server` or RHEL/CentOS without sudo) skips the apt
99	prereqs and Linuxbrew, falling back to per-tool curl-installers and
100	GitHub releases — coverage is intentionally narrower (no GUI, no
101	system-wide installs).
102	
103	---
104	
105	## Per-manager catalog
106	
107	Each subsection below covers one manager. Format:
108	
109	- **Owns** — what tools end up under this manager's control
110	- **How a tool gets there** — the canonical "I want to add tool X via this manager" recipe
111	- **Per-OS notes** — branching when relevant
112	- **Upgrade path** — link to the matching category in `upgrades.md`
113	
114	The ansible roles section is split into thematic subsections because
115	26 roles in one table is unreadable.
116	
117	### 1. Bootstrap scripts (pre-chezmoi)
118	
119	**Files**: `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl`,
120	`run_once_before_02_fix_intel_homebrew.sh.tmpl`,
121	`run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`
122	
123	**Owns** — the four foundational managers that everything else
124	assumes:
125	
126	| Tool | Mechanism | Per-OS |
127	|---|---|---|
128	| **Homebrew** | `Homebrew/install` curl script | macOS always; Linux only when `installBrewApps=true` & non-noRoot & arch∈{amd64,arm64}. Mirrors via `HOMEBREW_*_GIT_REMOTE` (Aliyun / USTC / BFSU / TUNA) when `useChineseMirror=true` |
129	| **uv** | `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh \| sh` | all OSes if missing |
130	| **mise** | `curl https://mise.run \| sh`, with direct `mise.jdx.dev/mise-latest-linux-${arch}[-musl]` fallback (musl forced when glibc < 2.28) | all OSes; arch detection (x64/arm64/armv7) |
131	| **ansible-core** | `uv tool install --force --python 3.13 ansible-core` | all OSes; force-refreshes if existing ansible runs on Python < 3.10 |
132	| **ansible-galaxy: community.general** | `ansible-galaxy collection install --force-with-deps` | all OSes |
133	| **mise runtimes** | `mise install --yes` (consumes `~/.config/mise/config.toml`) | all OSes — see [§ mise](#4-mise-runtime-versions) |
134	
135	**Linux prereqs (apt)** to make Linuxbrew + mise Ruby + ansible-cryptography
136	buildable: `build-essential`, `procps`, `curl`, `file`, `git` (always);
137	`libffi-dev`, `libyaml-dev`, `python3-dev` (non-noRoot only).
138	
139	**Intel-Mac-only side script**: `run_once_before_02_fix_intel_homebrew.sh.tmpl`
140	runs `softwareupdate -i` for Xcode CLT, then `brew cleanup` +
141	`brew link --overwrite git`.
142	
143	**One-shot migrations**: `run_once_before_50_opencode_migrate.sh.tmpl`
144	moves a legacy config file (`~/.config/opencode/config.json` →
145	`opencode.json`). Not an install.
146	
147	**Adding to bootstrap**: only when the new tool is required *before*
148	ansible runs — e.g. ansible itself, mise (because ansible roles call
149	`mise exec`), uv (because some roles call `uv tool install`). Otherwise
150	prefer an ansible role.
151	
152	### 2. Homebrew (formulae + casks)
153	
154	Three Brewfile templates + scattered `community.general.homebrew[_cask]`
155	tasks in ansible roles. The split is **macOS-centric**: Linux Brewfile is
156	empty, Linuxbrew use happens role-by-role.
157	
158	#### 2.1 Brewfiles
159	
160	| File | Owns |
161	|---|---|
162	| `Brewfile.tmpl` (shared) | Taps: `nikitabobko/tap`. Formulae (macOS-only via inner `{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" }}`): `mas`, `tailscale` |
163	| `Brewfile.darwin.tmpl` | All GUI casks — see table below |
164	| `Brewfile.linux.tmpl` | Empty (commented-out placeholders only) |
165	
166	**macOS casks** (~25 active, gated by feature flags):
167	
168	| Cask | Gating |
169	|---|---|
170	| `alacritty`, `warp`, `cmux`, `cursor`, `visual-studio-code` | always |
171	| `claude`, `opencode-desktop`, `antigravity` | `installAiDesktopApps` |
172	| `chatgpt`, `codex-app` | `installAiDesktopApps` + arm64 |
173	| `codeisland` (tap `wxtsky/tap`) | `installAiDesktopApps` |
174	| `ollama-app` | `installAiDesktopApps` + `installLlmTools` |
175	| `nikitabobko/tap/aerospace`, `alt-tab`, `raycast`, `maccy`, `scroll-reverser`, `the-unarchiver`, `applite` | always (system utilities) |
176	| `discord` | always |
177	| `arc` | always |
178	| `obsidian`, `google-drive`, `grammarly-desktop`, `super-productivity` | always |
179	| `spotify`, `anki` | always |
180	| `tailscale-app` | always |
181	| `dbeaver-community` | always |
182	| `superset` | arm64 only |
183	
184	Many more entries exist in commented-out form (steam, telegram,
185	openvpn-connect, etc.) — uncomment to enable.
186	
187	#### 2.2 Role-driven brew (formulae + casks)
188	
189	Most CLI formulae land via ansible roles, not the Brewfile. Examples:
190	
191	- `base/tasks/main.yml`: `git`, `git-lfs`, `curl`, `wget`, `ripgrep`, `fd`, `jq`, `tree`, `just`
192	- `devtools/tasks/main.yml`: large set — `bat`, `gh`, `glab`, `diffnav`, `git-delta`, `eza`, `tlrc`, `glow`, `gum`, `vhs`, `freeze`, `thefuck`, `zoxide`, `direnv`, `yazi`, `superfile`, `tmux`, `sesh`, `worktrunk`, `workmux`, `zellij`, `btop`, `htop`, `duckdb`, `rclone`, `coreutils`, `taplo`, `television`, `pandoc`, `tailspin`, `lnav`, `grc`, `dasel`, `yq`, `jnv`, `witr`, `figlet`, `toilet`, `lolcat`, `fastfetch`, `shellcheck`, `shfmt`, `bats-core`, `git-graph`
193	- `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml`: `claude-code` (cask), `codex` (cask), `gemini-cli` (formula), `rtk` (formula), `specstory`, `codexbar`, `td`, `sidecar` (all with tap setup)
194	- `networking_tools/`: `nmap`, `arp-scan`, `mtr`, `iperf3`, `doggo`, `httpie`, `gping`, `trippy`, `bandwhich`, `rustscan`, `speedtest` (tap `teamookla/speedtest`), `ngrok`, `cloudflared`
195	- `media_tools/`: `ffmpeg`, `imagemagick`, `exiftool`, `vips`
196	- `iac_tools/`: `azure-cli`, `hashicorp/tap/terraform`, `opentofu`
197	- `llm_tools/`: `llmfit`, `models`, `ollama`
198	- `security_tools/`: `gitleaks`, `go`
199	- `starship/`, `atuin/`, `neovim/`, `bash/` (gawk), `zsh/` — each installs its primary tool via homebrew formula on macOS
200	- `pueue` (from `rust_cargo_tools/`): macOS uses homebrew formula
201	
202	**Per-OS dispatch** is the universal pattern in roles: macOS branch uses
203	`community.general.homebrew` / `homebrew_cask`; Linux branches use apt,
204	Linuxbrew (when present), or GitHub releases. See each role for the
205	explicit `when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"` guard.
206	
207	**Tap inventory** (added by various roles): `nikitabobko/tap`,
208	`wxtsky/tap` (CodeIsland), `hashicorp/tap` (terraform),
209	`teamookla/speedtest`, `specstoryai/tap`, `steipete/tap` (CodexBar),
210	`marcus/tap` (td, sidecar), `dlvhdr/formulae`, `raine/workmux`.
211	
212	**Adding via homebrew**: prefer a brew formula/cask only when the tool
213	is macOS-shipped and Linux equivalents go via apt or release tarball.
214	Linux-first tools rarely belong in the Brewfile.
215	
216	#### 2.3 Homebrew prefix dispatch helper
217	
218	`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::_uv_install_style` (and mirrored helpers in
219	`python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`) inspect whether a binary lives under
220	`brew --prefix` to decide between `brew upgrade <pkg>` and the tool's
221	native self-update. This avoids the "I `uv self update` on a brew-uv
222	host and silently no-op" trap — see
223	[`pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md).
224	
225	### 3. Ansible roles
226	
227	26 roles under `dot_ansible/roles/`. Triggered by
228	`.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`
229	(re-runs when any role's `tasks/main.yml` or `defaults/main.yml` changes
230	— SHA256-tracked).
231	
232	**Universal patterns**:
233	
234	- `state: present` / `creates:` — install-only, no silent upgrades
235	- Per-OS branching via `when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"` (or `["Debian", "RedHat"]`)
236	- `tags: [sudo]` on any `become: true` task (so noRoot mode skips them — see [`pitfalls/ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md))
237	- `failed_when: false` + `register:` for "is the tool installed?" probes
238	- Linux user-level fallback to `~/.local/bin` when distro package is missing or too old (handles RHEL/CentOS + noRoot + Apple-Silicon-not-bottled scenarios)
239	
240	**Role feature flags** (set in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` via prompts):
241	`installBrewApps`, `installAiDesktopApps`, `installCodingAgents`,
242	`installLlmTools`, `installPythonUvTools`, `installJsCliTools`,
243	`installDotnetTools`, `installIacTools`, `installMediaTools`,
244	`installNetworkingTools`, `installTunnelTools`, `installBitwarden`,
245	`installInputMethod`, `installAuditd`. Roles gate themselves on the
246	matching flag; the bundle script `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` defines
247	profile presets (`minimal`, `cloud-vm` planned, default-developer, …).
248	
249	#### 3.1 Base / shared CLI
250	
251	| Role | Owns | Per-OS mechanism |
252	|---|---|---|
253	| `base` | `git`, `git-lfs`, `curl`, `wget`, `ripgrep`, `fd`, `jq`, `tree`, `just`, `gcc`/`build-essential`/`make` | macOS: brew formulae · Debian: apt (`fd-find` + `/usr/bin/fd` symlink) · RedHat: yum · `just` always via `curl https://just.systems/install.sh` · Linux user-level GitHub-release fallback to `~/.local/bin` for ripgrep/fd/jq/git-lfs |
254	| `homebrew` | (no installs — refresh + cleanup only, 24h-throttled) | n/a |
255	| `atuin` | `atuin` shell history sync | macOS: brew formula · Linux: `curl https://setup.atuin.sh \| sh -s -- --non-interactive` → `~/.atuin/bin/` |
256	| `nerdfonts` | `font-hack-nerd-font` | macOS: brew cask · Linux: download `Hack.zip` from `nerd-fonts/releases/latest` → `~/.local/share/fonts` + `fc-cache -fv` |
257	
258	#### 3.2 Shells (`bash`, `zsh`, `starship`)
259	
260	| Role | Owns | Per-OS mechanism |
261	|---|---|---|
262	| `bash` | `gawk` (ble.sh dep, unconditional); homebrew `bash` 5.x + `/etc/shells` + `chsh` (macOS only when `primary_shell="bash"`) | macOS: brew · Debian: apt · RedHat: yum |
263	| `zsh` | system `zsh` package; **source-build zsh 5.9** to `~/.local` on RHEL/CentOS 7 if system zsh < 5.3; `chsh` when `primary_shell="zsh"` (default) | macOS: brew · Debian: apt · RedHat: yum + ncurses-devel source build fallback. oh-my-zsh + plugins ship as externals (§12) |
264	| `starship` | `starship` prompt | macOS: brew formula · Linux: `curl https://starship.rs/install.sh \| sh -s -- --yes` → sudo `/usr/local/bin` → user `~/.local/bin` fallback |
265	
266	The `primaryShell` chezmoi prompt gates the `chsh` call only — both
267	shells deploy their configs everywhere. See AGENTS.md → "`primaryShell`
268	choice gates `chsh` only" hard invariant.
269	
270	#### 3.3 DevTools (mega-role)
271	
272	Single role, ~50 tools — the kitchen sink for terminal-life CLIs.
273	There's a backlog item ([`backlog/devtools-role-split.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/devtools-role-split.md))
274	considering whether to break this up.
275	
276	**macOS** (homebrew, taps: `dlvhdr/formulae` for `gh-dash`,
277	`raine/workmux`): `bat`, `bats-core`, `gh`, `glab`, `diffnav`, `git-delta`,
278	`git-graph`, `eza`, `tlrc`, `glow`, `gum`, `vhs`, `freeze`, `thefuck`,
279	`zoxide`, `direnv`, `yazi`, `superfile`, `tmux`, `sesh`, `worktrunk`,
280	`workmux`, `zellij`, `btop`, `htop`, `duckdb`, `rclone`, `coreutils`,
281	`taplo`, `television`, `pandoc`, `tailspin`, `lnav`, `grc`, `dasel`,
282	`yq`, `jnv`, `witr`, `figlet`, `toilet`, `lolcat`, `fastfetch`,
283	`shellcheck`, `shfmt`.
284	
285	**Linux** — per-tool dispatch. The pattern is **apt/yum (system) →
286	GitHub release tarball or installer (user)**:
287	
288	| Tool | Linux mechanism (preferred → fallback) |
289	|---|---|
290	| `gh` | GitHub `.deb` → user tarball |
291	| `glab` | GitHub `.deb` → user tarball |
292	| `bat` | apt + `/usr/bin/bat` symlink → GitHub musl release |
293	| `bats` | apt → GitHub release `install.sh` |
294	| `zoxide` | `curl install.sh` |
295	| `eza` | gierens.de apt repo → user GitHub musl → brew aarch64 |
296	| `git-delta` | `.deb` (x86_64) → brew aarch64 → user GitHub musl |
297	| `diffnav` | user GitHub release |
298	| `gh-dash` | `gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash` |
299	| `git-graph` | user GitHub release (x86_64 only) |
300	| `tldr` | system npm or `mise exec -- npm install -g tldr` |

395	### 4. mise (runtime versions)
396	
397	**Config**: `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl`
398	
399	`[settings]`: `ruby.compile = false`.
400	
401	**Modern hosts** (default):
402	
403	| Runtime | Version |
404	|---|---|
405	| `node` | `lts` |
406	| `bun` | `latest` |
407	| `rust` | `latest` |
408	| `dotnet` | `latest` |
409	| `ruby` | `3` |
410	
411	Ruby is **skipped in noRoot mode** (`profile=ubuntu_server` without
412	sudo) because it needs `libffi-dev` / `libyaml-dev` to build, which
413	require apt.
414	
415	**oldEL (CentOS/RHEL 7, glibc 2.17)**: only `ruby = "3"` — other
416	runtimes have glibc/libstdc++ requirements too new for EL7.
417	
418	**Upgrade**: `just upgrade-mise` → `mise self-update --yes` + `mise upgrade`
419	(honours the version constraints in the config; `lts`/`latest` move
420	forward, pinned versions don't).
421	
422	**Adding a runtime**: edit `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl` directly.
423	Runtime-version gating across hosts is on the [backlog](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/mise-runtime-gating.md).
424	
425	**Why mise (not nvm/rbenv/pyenv/asdf/n)**: unified, language-agnostic,
426	respects `.tool-versions`, doesn't fight shell init order. Python is
427	deliberately **not** mise-managed — that's uv's territory (faster + no
428	build-from-source for CPython, which the noRoot Linux path can't do).
429	The [backlog](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/mise-runtime-gating.md) tracks
430	finer-grained per-host gating.
431

471	- `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml:1153-1184` — `specify-cli` (from `git+...`)

479	If the package writes companion binaries beyond the entry point, declare
480	**both** `with_executables_from:` AND `extra_binaries:` — otherwise the
481	install guard short-circuits on hosts where the primary binary already
482	exists and shims are never written ([`pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md)).
483	If gcc < 9 is in scope, set `needs_modern_gcc: true`.

485	### 6. npm (global Node CLIs)
486	
487	**Config**: `dot_ansible/roles/js_cli_tools/defaults/main.yml` for the
488	JS-tools-specific list. Scattered global-npm installs live in other
489	roles (`coding_agents`, `bitwarden`, `lazyvim_deps`, `devtools`).
490	
491	**Install dispatch** (universal pattern across roles):
492	
493	```yaml
494	# On Linux:
495	mise exec -- npm install -g <package>
496	# Falls back to system npm if mise has no node registered
497	# On macOS:
498	community.general.npm: { name: <package>, global: true }
499	```
500	
501	Linux explicitly uses `mise exec -- npm` to avoid the Ubuntu apt npm
502	(too old; system Node 12 fails `engine` checks for modern packages and
503	`/usr/local/lib/node_modules` is root-owned, breaking `--global` for
504	non-root users). See [`pitfalls/ansible-js-cli-tools-old-system-node.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/ansible-js-cli-tools-old-system-node.md).
505	
506	**Inventory**:
507	
508	| Package | Binary | Role / line |
509	|---|---|---|
510	| `readability-cli` | `readable` | `js_cli_tools/defaults/main.yml` |
511	| `@bitwarden/cli` | `bw` | `bitwarden/tasks/main.yml` |
512	| `@githubnext/github-copilot-cli` | `github-copilot-cli` | `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml:134-168` |
513	| `@openai/codex` | `codex` (Linux only — macOS uses brew cask) | `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml:172-236` |
514	| `@google/gemini-cli` | `gemini` (Linux always; macOS fallback if brew formula fails) | `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml:240-300` |
515	| `@openchamber/web` | `openchamber` | `coding_agents/tasks/main.yml:1188-1222` |
516	| `tldr` | `tldr` (Linux only — macOS uses `tlrc` via brew) | `devtools/tasks/main.yml` |
517	| `tree-sitter-cli` | `tree-sitter` | `lazyvim_deps/tasks/main.yml` (preferred over cargo fallback) |
518	
519	**Upgrade**: `just upgrade-npm` → `npm -g update` with `mise exec --`
520	fallback.
521	
522	**Adding an npm tool**: append to `js_cli_tools/defaults/main.yml` (for
523	general utilities); for an agent CLI, add the install task to
524	`coding_agents/tasks/main.yml` matching the existing dispatch pattern
525	(macOS via system npm, Linux via `mise exec -- npm install -g`).

527	### 7. cargo (Rust crates)
528	
529	**Config**: `dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/defaults/main.yml`
530	(currently `cargo_tools: []` — no generic entries).
531	
532	**Rust install**: `mise install rust@latest` (preferred), with two
533	fallback layers on noRoot/oldEL boxes: direct `rustup-init`, then
534	`https://static.rust-lang.org` when the configured mirror's manifest
535	is stale.
536	
537	**Inventory** (hard-coded in `tasks/main.yml`):
538	
539	| Crate | Mechanism | Notes |
540	|---|---|---|
541	| `recon` | `cargo install --git https://github.com/gavraz/recon --locked` | git source (no crates.io publish yet) |
542	| `pueue` | macOS brew formula; Linux `cargo install pueue --locked` | + `pueued.service` systemd user unit; version check `pueue_min_version=4.0.0` (warn-only) |
543	| `tree-sitter-cli` | `cargo install tree-sitter-cli` (fallback only) | preferred path is `mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli`; cargo path installs `libclang-dev`/`clang-devel` first |
544	| `alacritty` | cargo build (`gui_apps_linux`) | requires apt build deps (`cmake`, `pkg-config`, `libfontconfig1-dev`, `libxcb-xfixes0-dev`, `libxkbcommon-dev`) |
545	| `modelsdev` | cargo fallback (`llm_tools`) | only when Linuxbrew not present + brew formula `models` not available |
546	| `cargo-update` | `cargo install cargo-update` (bootstrap for upgrade) | installed by `upgrade_tools.sh::cat_cargo` on first run, then `cargo install-update -a` uses it |
547	
548	**Upgrade**: `just upgrade-cargo` → `cargo install-update -a` (which
549	covers everything installed via cargo, including pueue on Linux).
550	
551	**Adding a cargo tool**: prefer `cargo_tools: [<name>]` in the defaults
552	YAML (covered by `cargo install-update -a`); hard-code in `tasks/main.yml`
553	only when the install needs extra build deps or a non-crates.io source
554	(see `recon`, `pueue`).

600	### 10. curl-installer (self-managed CLIs)
601	
602	Tools that ship via vendor `install.sh` instead of any package manager.
603	Mostly the AI coding agents (each vendor maintains their own installer
604	+ self-update subcommand). All landing paths are user-writable so
605	in-binary self-update works without sudo.
606	
607	**Inventory**:
608	
609	| Tool | Install URL | Lands at | Source role |
610	|---|---|---|---|
611	| Homebrew | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/brew` (macOS) / `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/` (Linux) | bootstrap |
612	| uv | `https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh` | `~/.local/bin/uv` (or `~/.cargo/bin/uv`) | bootstrap |
613	| mise | `https://mise.run` | `~/.local/bin/mise` | bootstrap |
614	| just | `https://just.systems/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/just` or `~/.local/bin/just` | `base` |
615	| starship | `https://starship.rs/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/starship` or `~/.local/bin/starship` | `starship` |
616	| atuin | `https://setup.atuin.sh` | `~/.atuin/bin/atuin` | `atuin` |
617	| docker | `https://get.docker.com` | system docker (rootless variant) | `docker` (Linux) |
618	| zoxide | (vendor installer) | `~/.local/bin/zoxide` | `devtools` (Linux fallback) |
619	| direnv | (vendor installer) | `~/.local/bin/direnv` | `devtools` (Linux fallback) |
620	| **Claude Code** | `https://claude.ai/install.sh` | `~/.claude/local/bin/claude` | `coding_agents` (Linux) |
621	| **OpenCode** | `https://opencode.ai/install` (+ `--no-modify-path`) | `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` | `coding_agents` (macOS + Linux) |
622	| **Cursor CLI** | `https://cursor.com/install` | `~/.local/bin/cursor-agent` | `coding_agents` |
623	| **Antigravity CLI** | `https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh` (patched `--skip-path --skip-aliases`) | `~/.local/bin/agy` + `agyc` symlink | `coding_agents` |
624	| **RTK** | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/master/install.sh` | `~/.local/bin/rtk` | `coding_agents` (Linux) |
625	| **llmfit** | `https://llmfit.axjns.dev/install.sh` | `~/.local/bin/llmfit` (or system) | `llm_tools` (Linux) |
626	| **Ollama** | `https://ollama.com/install.sh` | system path (Linux, sudo) | `llm_tools` (Linux) |
627	| Ookla speedtest | `https://install.speedtest.net/app/cli/install.<distro>.sh` | system | `networking_tools` (Linux) |
628	
629	**Why curl-installer over a package manager**:
630	
631	- Fast-moving releases — vendor controls cadence (Claude, OpenCode,
632	  Cursor, Antigravity push daily/weekly)
633	- Self-update subcommand exists and the installer is the canonical
634	  reinstall path → `cat_agents` in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` can call
635	  either
636	- Avoids the "brew formula is 3 weeks stale" problem (see commit
637	  history for the OpenCode move from `anomalyco/tap` to official
638	  installer)
639	- No tap/PPA/repo to maintain
640	
641	**Adding a curl-installer tool**:
642	
643	1. Pick a role (or add to `coding_agents` if it's an agent)
644	2. Use the canonical pattern: `which` check → `creates:` guard on the
645	   binary path → `curl ... | bash [-s -- --no-modify-path]` shell task
646	3. If the installer mutates shell rc files, add a `--no-modify-path`
647	   flag (or equivalent — see OpenCode and Antigravity blocks). The
648	   chezmoi-managed PATH is the SSOT
649	4. Update `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_agents` if the tool has a
650	   self-update subcommand (or just an installer-as-upgrader path)
651	5. If the binary lands somewhere other than `~/.local/bin` (e.g.
652	   `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`), add an existence-gated PATH prepend
653	   to `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl`
654	
655	### 11. GitHub-release downloads (user-level fallback)
656	
657	When apt/yum can't satisfy a version requirement (e.g. Apple Silicon
658	brew bottle missing, RHEL/CentOS package too old, noRoot host with no
659	sudo), roles fall back to downloading the latest GitHub release tarball
660	and extracting to `~/.local/bin` (user-writable, already on PATH).
661	
662	**Canonical pattern**:
663	
664	```yaml
665	- name: Get latest <tool> release
666	  ansible.builtin.uri:
667	    url: https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest
668	    return_content: true
669	  register: <tool>_release
670	
671	- name: Compute <tool> arch
672	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
673	    <tool>_arch: "{{ 'amd64' if target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64'] else 'arm64' if ... else 'unsupported' }}"
674	
675	- name: Download / extract / copy into ~/.local/bin
676	  block:
677	    - get_url: { url: "https://github.com/.../{{ tag }}/{{ asset }}", dest: /tmp/..., retries: 3, delay: 5, timeout: 120 }
678	    - unarchive: { src: ..., dest: /tmp/..., remote_src: true }
679	    - find:      { paths: /tmp/..., patterns: <binary>, file_type: file }
680	    - copy:      { src: ..., dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/<binary>", mode: '0755' }
681	  rescue:
682	    - debug: "<tool> installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
683	```
684	
685	**Tools using this pattern** (rough list — see each role's `tasks/main.yml`):
686	
687	- `base`: `ripgrep`, `fd`, `jq`, `git-lfs`
688	- `devtools`: `gh`, `glab`, `bat`, `bats`, `eza`, `git-delta`, `diffnav`, `git-graph`, `glow`, `gum`, `vhs`, `freeze`, `duckdb`, `yazi`, `superfile`, `btop`, `zellij`, `sesh`, `worktrunk`, `workmux`, `taplo`, `tv` (television), `lnav`, `tailspin`, `dasel`, `yq`, `jnv`, `witr`
689	- `networking_tools`: `doggo`, `gping`, `trippy`, `bandwhich`, `rustscan`, `cloudflared`
690	- `neovim`: nvim tarball
691	- `lazyvim_deps`: `lazygit` fallback
692	- `coding_agents`: `specstory`, `codexbar`, `td`, `sidecar`, `agy` (all also have brew formula / cask as primary)
693	- `security_tools`: `gitleaks`
694	- `iac_tools`: `terraform`, `opentofu` user fallback (zip from `releases.hashicorp.com` / GitHub)
695	- `gui_apps_linux`: `AppImageLauncher Lite`, Zen Browser AppImage
696	- `bitwarden`: Desktop `.deb` fallback (Linux)
697	
698	**⚠️ Coverage gap**: GitHub-release downloads use a `creates:` guard
699	on the binary path, so once installed they're **never refreshed by
700	`chezmoi apply`** — and `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` has no category for
701	them. The only way to refresh: `rm` the binary, re-apply. See
702	[§ Coverage gaps](#coverage-gaps-install-only-no-automated-upgrade)
703	below.
704	
705	**Adding a GitHub-release tool**: copy the canonical block from
706	e.g. `devtools/tasks/main.yml` (look for an existing tool with a
707	similar arch matrix), substitute owner/repo/asset-name. Always wrap in
708	`block:` / `rescue:` (vendor-side outages happen) and use
709	`retries: 3, delay: 5, timeout: 120` on the download.
710	
711	### 12. chezmoi externals (refresh-periodic git/file fetches)
712
```
</details></tool-use>
