```text
1	# Shared Storage — Cluster Filesystems and Network Mounts
2	
3	Reference for "multiple machines need to see the same bytes." Picks a filesystem or protocol based on workload shape (POSIX vs object, HPC vs general, Linux-only vs mixed OS) and how much operational complexity you're willing to absorb.
4	
5	## Quick answer
6	
7	| Problem | Pick |
8	|---------|------|
9	| Shared `/home` for 5-20 Linux users on a LAN | [NFSv4](#nfsv4) (simplest); pair with [autofs](#client-mount-recipes) |
10	| Same but with Mac/Windows clients | [Samba (SMB/CIFS)](#smbcifs-samba) |
11	| HPC / ML research lab, many nodes, high throughput | [BeeGFS](#beegfs) or [Lustre](#lustre) |
12	| You already run Ceph and need a POSIX FS too | [CephFS](#cephfs) |
13	| Small team, want scale-out NAS, simple ops | [MooseFS](#moosefs--lizardfs) / [SeaweedFS](#seaweedfs) / [JuiceFS](#juicefs) |
14	| Just want S3-compatible object store | [MinIO](https://min.io) / [Ceph RGW](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/radosgw/) / SeaweedFS |
15	| Sync cloud storage onto local path (per-user) | [rclone](https://rclone.org) (already installed in this repo, see [README.md](../../README.md)) |
16	
17	## The landscape
18	
19	| System | License | Type | POSIX | Metadata | Client | Op complexity | Best for |
20	|--------|---------|------|-------|----------|--------|---------------|----------|
21	| [NFSv4](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7530) | Open standard | Network FS | Yes | Server-side | Kernel (all OSes) | Low | Shared home dirs, config, small clusters |
22	| [Samba (SMB/CIFS)](https://www.samba.org) | GPLv3 | Network FS | Mostly | Server-side | Kernel (all OSes incl. Windows) | Low | Mixed-OS desktops |
23	| [CephFS](https://docs.ceph.com/en/latest/cephfs/) | LGPLv2.1 | Distributed POSIX FS | Yes | Distributed (MDS) | Kernel or FUSE | High (MON/MGR/OSD/MDS) | Unified object+block+FS; K8s via [Rook](https://rook.io) |
24	| [BeeGFS](https://www.beegfs.io) | Open core (community edition free) | Parallel FS | Yes | Distributed metadata servers | Kernel module | Medium | HPC, high metadata ops/sec |
25	| [Lustre](https://www.lustre.org) | GPLv2 | Parallel FS | Yes | MDS + OSTs | Kernel module | Very high | Extreme bandwidth HPC (TOP500) |
26	| [GlusterFS](https://www.gluster.org) | GPLv2/LGPLv3 | Distributed FS | Yes | Client-hashed | FUSE or native | Medium | Scale-out NAS (declining; see notes) |
27	| [MooseFS / LizardFS](https://moosefs.com) | GPLv2 / BSD | Distributed FS | Yes | Single master + shadows | FUSE | Low-medium | Simple "big NAS" |
28	| [SeaweedFS](https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs) | Apache 2.0 | Distributed FS + object | Yes (FUSE) | Distributed | FUSE or S3 | Medium | Billions of small files |
29	| [JuiceFS](https://juicefs.com) | Apache 2.0 / commercial | POSIX-on-object | Yes | Redis / TiKV / MySQL | FUSE | Low | POSIX FS backed by S3/MinIO |
30	| [MinIO](https://min.io) | AGPLv3 / commercial | Object store | No (S3 only) | Distributed | S3 SDK | Low | S3-compatible object storage |
31	| [OpenZFS](https://openzfs.org) | CDDL | Local/replicated FS | Yes | Local | Native | Low per-host | Single-node NAS; pair with NFS/Samba for sharing |
32	
33	## Per-system notes
34	
35	### NFSv4
36	
37	The simplest, most universal network filesystem. Every Unix and Mac already has a client.
38	
39	- Server-side: Linux `nfs-kernel-server` + `/etc/exports`. One server is a SPOF; scale by moving to NFS-Ganesha (userspace) fronting Ceph/GlusterFS, or by sharding users across servers.
40	- Security: NFSv4 supports Kerberos (`sec=krb5p`). Without it, UIDs are trusted on the wire — bad on untrusted networks.
41	- Locking: NFSv4 has proper POSIX locks (unlike NFSv3). Still, databases and some build systems (bazel, cargo on shared cache) hate NFS; keep fast-mutation workloads local.
42	- Use cases: shared `/home`, shared configs, SSO-authenticated read-mostly corpora, HPC scratch when bandwidth isn't the bottleneck.
43	
44	### SMB/CIFS (Samba)
45	
46	SMB3 is the protocol Windows speaks natively. Linux and macOS both speak it as clients.
47	
48	- Server: `smbd` on Linux, configured in `/etc/samba/smb.conf`. Can join an AD domain.
49	- Strong for mixed OS environments; supports per-user ACLs that map to Windows ACLs.
50	- Weaker than NFS for dense small-file POSIX workloads; better for "department shared drive."
51	
52	### CephFS
53	
54	CephFS is the POSIX-filesystem API on top of Ceph, alongside RBD (block) and RGW (object/S3). All three ride on the same RADOS object store.
55	
56	- Operational cost: a Ceph cluster is MON + MGR + OSD + (for FS) MDS daemons across at least 3 nodes. Day-2 expertise non-trivial (PGs, CRUSH maps, OSD rebalancing).
57	- Strength: one cluster, three APIs. Your K8s persistent volumes (RBD), your S3 (RGW), and your shared FS (CephFS) all share the same redundancy and pool.
58	- Client: mainline kernel client (`mount -t ceph`) or FUSE fallback. Works out of the box on modern Linux.
59	- Kubernetes: [Rook](https://rook.io) operator makes Ceph-on-K8s ergonomic; CephFS-CSI mounts volumes into pods.
60	- Best for: you already need object + block and want FS "for free."
61	
62	### BeeGFS
63	
64	Originally Fraunhofer ITWM, now ThinkParQ. Widely used in HPC and ML training clusters because of its metadata architecture (multiple metadata servers balance load, unlike Lustre's single-MDS classic layout).
65	
66	- Components: management, metadata, storage, client. All userspace except the client kernel module.
67	- Free for community use (open source), enterprise support from ThinkParQ.
68	- Strong fit when users have millions of small files (typical ML datasets).
69	- Commonly combined with SLURM + FreeIPA as the "lab cluster" stack — see [compute-scheduling.md](compute-scheduling.md) and [shared-home-identity.md](shared-home-identity.md).
70	
71	### Lustre
72	
73	The "if you have to ask, you don't need it" option. Powers most TOP500 supercomputers.
74	
75	- Extreme bandwidth, great for sequential HPC IO.
76	- Kernel-module client, coupled to specific kernel versions.
77	- Requires dedicated sysadmins. Not a DIY choice.
78	- If you're not at >PB scale across >100 nodes, pick BeeGFS instead.
79	
80	### GlusterFS
81	
82	Scale-out NAS with FUSE or native client.
83	
84	- Historically popular, but [RedHat ended RHGS in 2024](https://access.redhat.com/announcements/7019004) and upstream contributions have slowed. Evaluate carefully for greenfield projects.
85	- Still fine for existing deployments; migration path to CephFS is the common recommendation.
86	
87	### MooseFS / LizardFS
88	
89	Single-master distributed FS with FUSE client. LizardFS is a community fork (older; less active now).
90	
91	- Simple mental model: master + chunk servers + FUSE clients.
92	- Good for "big NAS for a small team" without Ceph complexity.
93	- Master is a SPOF unless you run shadow masters (Pro edition).
94	
95	### SeaweedFS
96	
97	Object-first, but exposes a FUSE POSIX layer.
98	
99	- Optimized for billions of small files (Facebook Haystack-inspired).
100	- Has S3, HDFS, FUSE, WebDAV frontends.
101	- Lighter ops than Ceph. Active community.
102	
103	### JuiceFS
104	
105	Interesting hybrid: POSIX FS metadata in Redis/TiKV/MySQL, data in any S3-compatible object store.
106	
107	- Mount on any client, back onto cheap cloud object storage.
108	- Metadata in a DB you already run.
109	- Good for "I want a POSIX FS but pay object-store prices" and for cross-region shared FS.
110	
111	### OpenZFS on a single host + NFS/Samba export
112	
113	Not distributed, but worth naming: OpenZFS on one powerful server (ideally with replication via `zfs send` to a second box) + NFS/Samba export is the pragmatic answer for many teams.
114	
115	- Snapshot + send/receive + compression + integrity.
116	- Works under TrueNAS, on Proxmox host, on stock Ubuntu via `zfs-dkms`.
117	- Scales vertically, not horizontally.
118	
119	## Decision matrix by workload
120	
121	| Scenario | Pick | Why |
122	|----------|------|-----|
123	| Shared `/home` for 10-person team | NFSv4 + ZFS backing | Simplest; snapshot story via ZFS; good enough at this scale |
124	| GPU cluster, 20-100 nodes, ML training | BeeGFS | Fast metadata; handles millions of small dataset files |
125	| HPC cluster, MPI jobs, >100 nodes | Lustre or BeeGFS | Bandwidth; Lustre if you have dedicated FS admins |
126	| K8s cluster needing object + block + FS | CephFS + RBD + RGW via Rook | One storage layer for three APIs |
127	| Mixed Mac/Win/Linux office file share | Samba | Only one that native Windows speaks cleanly |
128	| "POSIX FS but cheap" | JuiceFS on S3 | Object-storage economics, POSIX semantics |
129	| "Big NAS, simple ops, Linux only" | MooseFS or SeaweedFS | Less complex than Ceph; no HPC needs |
130	| Single beefy NAS host | OpenZFS + NFS/Samba | Vertical scaling is fine; snapshots are king |
131	
132	## Client mount recipes
133	
134	### NFSv4 mount
135	
136	```bash
137	# One-off mount
138	sudo mount -t nfs -o vers=4.2 nas.example.com:/home /mnt/home
139	
140	# Persistent via /etc/fstab
141	echo 'nas.example.com:/home  /home  nfs  vers=4.2,hard,nconnect=8,_netdev  0 0' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
142	```
143	
144	### autofs for on-demand `/home`
145	
146	Standard pattern for a shared-home cluster — mount each user's home only when they log in.
147	
148	```bash
149	# /etc/auto.master.d/home.autofs
150	/home /etc/auto.home --timeout=600
151	
152	# /etc/auto.home
153	*  -fstype=nfs4,rw,hard,nconnect=8  nas.example.com:/home/&
154	```
155	
156	`&` is replaced by the requested subdirectory (username). See also [shared-home-identity.md](shared-home-identity.md).
157	
158	### CephFS mount
159	
160	```bash
161	# Kernel client, requires CephX secret file
162	sudo mount -t ceph user@.myfs=/ /mnt/cephfs \
163	  -o mon_addr=mon1.ceph:6789/mon2.ceph:6789,secretfile=/etc/ceph/client.user.secret
164	```
165	
166	### BeeGFS mount
167	
168	```bash
169	# After installing beegfs-client + beegfs-helperd packages, edit:
170	#   /etc/beegfs/beegfs-client.conf  -> set sysMgmtdHost
171	sudo systemctl enable --now beegfs-helperd beegfs-client
172	# Default mount point is /mnt/beegfs
173	```
174	
175	### SMB/CIFS
176	
177	```bash
178	sudo mount -t cifs //server/share /mnt/share \
179	  -o username=alice,uid=$(id -u),gid=$(id -g),vers=3.1.1,seal
180	```
181	
182	### rclone (S3 / WebDAV / GDrive as POSIX)
183	
184	```bash
185	rclone mount myremote: ~/mnt/myremote --vfs-cache-mode full --daemon
186	```
187	
188	Per-user, no root required. Good for cloud-backed personal working sets.
189	
190	## Storage for containers and K8s
191	
192	Shared storage often surfaces to workloads via CSI drivers:
193	
194	- [ceph-csi](https://github.com/ceph/ceph-csi) — CephFS + RBD
195	- [nfs-subdir-external-provisioner](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/nfs-subdir-external-provisioner) — dynamic PVs from a single NFS export
196	- [Longhorn](https://longhorn.io) — SUSE / Rancher block storage for K8s (replicated local disks)
197	- [OpenEBS](https://openebs.io) — per-node local PV + replicated engines
198	- [JuiceFS CSI](https://juicefs.com/docs/csi/introduction/) — POSIX mount backed by S3
199	
200	When containers need to share a volume across pods (RWX), you need a shared FS — typically CephFS, NFS, or JuiceFS. RBD and Longhorn are block-level (RWO).
```

```text
1	# rclone channel for television (tv).
2	# Browse configured remotes, drill into directories, preview about/size/config.
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   tv rclone
6	#   RCLONE_TV_PATH='remote:some/dir/' tv rclone   # drill straight in from CLI
7	#   RCLONE_TV_NOCACHE=1 tv rclone                 # bypass preview cache
8	#
9	# Source behavior:
10	#   $RCLONE_TV_PATH unset  -> `rclone listremotes`            (top-level)
11	#   $RCLONE_TV_PATH set    -> `rclone lsf "$RCLONE_TV_PATH"`  (drilled)
12	# The Enter action (actions:drill) sets $RCLONE_TV_PATH and re-execs `tv rclone`
13	# so drilling has no back-stack to maintain — Esc in the nested view returns to
14	# the parent picker because `mode = "execute"` pauses the outer TV until the
15	# nested process exits. Same pattern mlflow.toml uses for experiment-scoped
16	# runs, just with an env var instead of `--source-command` because the path
17	# already contains everything we need.
18	#
19	# Row format (TSV): <path>\t<kind>
20	#   kind ∈ {remote, dir, file}
21	# - For `listremotes` rows, kind is hardcoded `remote` and the path ends in `:`.
22	# - For `lsf` rows, kind is `dir` when the entry ends in `/`, else `file`.
23	#   The path is `$RCLONE_TV_PATH` concatenated with the entry, so deep drills
24	#   keep producing fully-qualified paths.
25	#
26	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
27	#   1. Default — about + top-level dirs (remote/dir rows) or lsjson (file rows)
28	#   2. Deeper  — `rclone lsd --max-depth 2 | head -200`
29	#   3. Flat    — `rclone lsf | head -200` (files + dirs mixed)
30	#   4. Config  — `rclone config show REMOTE`. Obscured tokens are
31	#                reversible base64, not encryption.
32	#
33	# Performance / caching:
34	#   All preview views cache results in /tmp/rclone-tv.UID/ keyed on
35	#   path+view, TTL 60s. Each rclone invocation also uses
36	#   --retries=1 --low-level-retries=1 --timeout=10s to fail fast — webdav
37	#   backends without quota API and Google Drive cold-start used to take
38	#   10-15s per preview without these. Set RCLONE_TV_NOCACHE=1 to bypass.
39	#   `rclone size` (recursive walk) is intentionally NOT in any default
40	#   preview — it's only on Alt+S.
41	#
42	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace avoids tmux/TV conflicts — see CLAUDE.md):
43	#   Enter      Drill (dir/remote) or paged lsjson (file)
44	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy path to clipboard (overrides TV default which copies full row)
45	#   Alt+A      `rclone about PATH --json` paged
46	#   Alt+S      `rclone size  PATH --json` paged (can be slow on large remotes)
47	#   Alt+B      `rclone ncdu  PATH` — full-screen TUI disk usage
48	#   Alt+C      `rclone config show REMOTE` paged
49	#   Alt+M      `mount | grep rclone` — active rclone/fuse mount status
50	
51	[metadata]
52	name = "rclone"
53	description = "rclone remotes: drill-in browser with about/size/config previews"
54	requirements = ["rclone"]
55	
56	[source]
57	command = """
58	if [ -n "${RCLONE_TV_PATH:-}" ]; then
59	  rclone lsf "$RCLONE_TV_PATH" --retries=1 --low-level-retries=1 --timeout=10s 2>/dev/null | awk -v p="$RCLONE_TV_PATH" '/\\/$/{print p$0"\\tdir";next}{print p$0"\\tfile"}'
60	else
61	  rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $0"\\tremote"}'
62	fi
63	"""
64	display = "{split:\\t:0}"
65	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
66	
67	[preview]
68	command = [
69	  """
70	sel='{split:\\t:0}'
71	kind='{split:\\t:1}'
72	cd="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rclone-tv.$(id -u)"
73	mkdir -p "$cd" 2>/dev/null
74	cf="$cd/$(printf '%s|v1' "$sel" | shasum | cut -c1-16)"
75	if [ -z "${RCLONE_TV_NOCACHE:-}" ] && [ -f "$cf" ] && [ "$(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -f %m "$cf" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$cf" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ))" -lt 60 ]; then
76	  cat "$cf"
77	else
78	  {
79	    case "$kind" in
80	      remote)
81	        printf '=== about ===\\n'
82	        rclone about "$sel" --json --retries=1 --low-level-retries=1 --timeout=10s 2>/dev/null | jq -C . 2>/dev/null || printf '(backend does not support `about`)\\n'
83	        printf '\\n=== top-level dirs ===\\n'
84	        rclone lsd "$sel" --max-depth 1 --retries=1 --low-level-retries=1 --timeout=10s 2>/dev/null | head -50 || printf '(empty or unreachable)\\n'
85	        ;;
86	      dir)
87	        printf '=== %s ===\\n' "$sel"
88	        rclone lsd "$sel" --max-depth 1 --retries=1 --low-level-retries=1 --timeout=10s 2>/dev/null | head -50
89	        printf '\\n[size: Alt+S | tree: Alt+B (ncdu)]\\n'
90	        ;;
91	      file)
92	        printf '=== %s (metadata) ===\\n' "$sel"
93	        rclone lsjson "$sel" --retries=1 --low-level-retries=1 --timeout=5s 2>/dev/null | jq -C . 2>/dev/null || printf '(lsjson failed)\\n'
94	        ;;
95	    esac
96	  } | tee "$cf"
97	fi
98	""",
99	  """
100	sel='{split:\\t:0}'
```

I now have a clear and somewhat surprising picture. Key findings before I confirm scope:

**The "Homebrew rclone doesn't support mount" premise is now outdated.** I tested the brew binary directly:
- `/opt/homebrew/bin/rclone mount --help` → **works** (rc=0). Modern Homebrew rclone (1.73+) is built with `cmount`/macFUSE support. So on current Homebrew, the brew rclone *does* support mount.
- You actually have **3 rclone binaries**: `~/.local/bin/rclone` v1.74.3 (official, wins on PATH), `/opt/homebrew/bin/rclone` v1.73.0 (brew), `/usr/local/bin/rclone` v1.70.3 (stray root-owned manual install).

**The real blocker for `rclone mount` on macOS is macFUSE, not rclone.** Your macFUSE is **4.10.2** (installed 2025-08-01) but macOS is **26.2** — the cask now ships **5.2.0**. macFUSE 4.x is rejected by macOS 26 → that's the "Unsupported macOS Version" dialog. macFUSE is **not managed by this repo** at all.

**The `chezmoi apply` failure is unrelated to rclone.** Homebrew 6.0 added a "trusted tap" security gate. Both your third-party taps are **Untrusted** (`raine/workmux` *and* `dlvhdr/formulae`), so `brew install` refuses to load their formulae. The install task failed on `workmux`; the next run would fail on `diffnav` too. Fix: add `brew trust` for both taps. The Linux rclone path already uses the official download to `~/.local/bin` (mount works with libfuse) — no change needed there.

Let me confirm scope on the two genuine decisions.

```md
# Fix Homebrew-6 tap-trust breakage + document rclone-mount/macFUSE reality on macOS

## Context

A `chezmoi update` on the Mac mini (macOS 26.2, Homebrew 6.0.2) failed the
`devtools` ansible role with:

\```
Error: Refusing to load formula raine/workmux/workmux from untrusted tap raine/workmux.
Run `brew trust --formula raine/workmux/workmux` or `brew trust raine/workmux` to trust it.
\```

**Homebrew 6.0 added a formula-trust security gate**: `brew install` now refuses
to load formulae from third-party taps until the tap is explicitly trusted. The
repo taps two third-party formulae in `devtools` — `raine/workmux` and
`dlvhdr/formulae` (diffnav) — and **both are currently `Untrusted`** (verified
via `brew tap-info`). The install task died on `workmux`; the next run would die
on `diffnav`. This blocks `chezmoi apply` entirely. **This is the must-fix.**

Separately, the user asked to review the rclone install method under the belief
"Homebrew rclone doesn't support mount." Investigation showed that premise is
**now outdated**:

- `/opt/homebrew/bin/rclone mount --help` works (rc=0) — modern Homebrew rclone
  (≥1.73) is built with `cmount`/macFUSE support. **Brew rclone supports mount on macOS today.**
- The machine has **3 rclone binaries**: `~/.local/bin/rclone` v1.74.3 (official,
  wins on PATH), `/opt/homebrew/bin/rclone` v1.73.0 (brew), `/usr/local/bin/rclone`
  v1.70.3 (stray root-owned manual install).
- The **real** blocker for `rclone mount` on macOS 26 is **macFUSE**: installed
  version is **4.10.2** (from 2025-08-01) but macOS 26.2 rejects it → the
  "Unsupported macOS Version" dialog. The cask now ships **5.2.0**. macFUSE is
  **not managed by this repo** at all.
- Linux rclone already installs the **official build** to `~/.local/bin`
  (`devtools/tasks/main.yml:1943-2022`) which supports mount via libfuse — no change needed.

**Decisions (confirmed with user):** keep brew rclone on macOS (no install-method
change — document the finding); document the macFUSE manual-upgrade path rather
than managing it in ansible (it needs a reboot + GUI security approval, which
violates the install-only philosophy); fix the tap-trust failure.

## Changes

### 1. Fix the Homebrew-6 untrusted-tap failure (blocking) — `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`

Insert a trust step **between** the two `homebrew_tap` tasks (lines 9–23) and the
`Install developer CLI tools (macOS)` task (line 25). `community.general.homebrew_tap`
has no trust parameter (feature is brand-new), so use `ansible.builtin.command`.

Idempotent + back-compatible (older Homebrew has no trust concept, so `tap-info`
won't contain `Untrusted` and the trust task no-ops — no need to version-gate):

\```yaml
- name: Check trust state of third-party taps (macOS, Homebrew >= 6.0 formula-trust gate)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"

## Approved Plan:
# Fix Homebrew-6 tap-trust breakage + document rclone-mount/macFUSE reality on macOS

## Context

A `chezmoi update` on the Mac mini (macOS 26.2, Homebrew 6.0.2) failed the
`devtools` ansible role with:

```
Error: Refusing to load formula raine/workmux/workmux from untrusted tap raine/workmux.
Run `brew trust --formula raine/workmux/workmux` or `brew trust raine/workmux` to trust it.
```

**Homebrew 6.0 added a formula-trust security gate**: `brew install` now refuses
to load formulae from third-party taps until the tap is explicitly trusted. The
repo taps two third-party formulae in `devtools` — `raine/workmux` and
`dlvhdr/formulae` (diffnav) — and **both are currently `Untrusted`** (verified
via `brew tap-info`). The install task died on `workmux`; the next run would die
on `diffnav`. This blocks `chezmoi apply` entirely. **This is the must-fix.**

Separately, the user asked to review the rclone install method under the belief
"Homebrew rclone doesn't support mount." Investigation showed that premise is
**now outdated**:

- `/opt/homebrew/bin/rclone mount --help` works (rc=0) — modern Homebrew rclone
  (≥1.73) is built with `cmount`/macFUSE support. **Brew rclone supports mount on macOS today.**
- The machine has **3 rclone binaries**: `~/.local/bin/rclone` v1.74.3 (official,
  wins on PATH), `/opt/homebrew/bin/rclone` v1.73.0 (brew), `/usr/local/bin/rclone`
  v1.70.3 (stray root-owned manual install).
- The **real** blocker for `rclone mount` on macOS 26 is **macFUSE**: installed
  version is **4.10.2** (from 2025-08-01) but macOS 26.2 rejects it → the
  "Unsupported macOS Version" dialog. The cask now ships **5.2.0**. macFUSE is
  **not managed by this repo** at all.
- Linux rclone already installs the **official build** to `~/.local/bin`
  (`devtools/tasks/main.yml:1943-2022`) which supports mount via libfuse — no change needed.

**Decisions (confirmed with user):** keep brew rclone on macOS (no install-method
change — document the finding); document the macFUSE manual-upgrade path rather
than managing it in ansible (it needs a reboot + GUI security approval, which
violates the install-only philosophy); fix the tap-trust failure.

## Changes

### 1. Fix the Homebrew-6 untrusted-tap failure (blocking) — `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`

Insert a trust step **between** the two `homebrew_tap` tasks (lines 9–23) and the
`Install developer CLI tools (macOS)` task (line 25). `community.general.homebrew_tap`
has no trust parameter (feature is brand-new), so use `ansible.builtin.command`.

Idempotent + back-compatible (older Homebrew has no trust concept, so `tap-info`
won't contain `Untrusted` and the trust task no-ops — no need to version-gate):

```yaml
- name: Check trust state of third-party taps (macOS, Homebrew >= 6.0 formula-trust gate)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew tap-info {{ item }}"
  loop:
    - dlvhdr/formulae
    - raine/workmux
  register: devtools_tap_info
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Trust untrusted third-party taps (macOS)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
    - "'Untrusted' in item.stdout"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew trust {{ item.item }}"
  loop: "{{ devtools_tap_info.results }}"
  loop_control:
    label: "{{ item.item }}"
  changed_when: true
```

Notes:
- Trust **both** taps — `dlvhdr/formulae` is also `Untrusted` and would fail on
  the next run otherwise.
- Keep this driven off the existing tap list; if a future third-party tap is
  added to this role, add it to the `loop` here too (call this out in the
  inline comment).
- This touches the `devtools` role which is surface #1 of the workmux status-icon
  6-file invariant in CLAUDE.md, but that invariant is about the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅`
  status mechanism — adding a tap-trust step does not affect it. No mirror update needed.

3	Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
4	when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool

14	
15	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
18	| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
19	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
20	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
21	| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |
22	
23	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
24	serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
25	recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
26	is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
27	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.

34	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared

# `chezmoi apply` aborts: Homebrew refuses to load a formula from an untrusted tap

**Symptoms** (grep this section):
- `Error: Refusing to load formula raine/workmux/workmux from untrusted tap raine/workmux.`
- `Run \`brew trust --formula raine/workmux/workmux\` or \`brew trust raine/workmux\` to trust it.`
- ansible `devtools : Install developer CLI tools (macOS)` task → `FAILED!` → `changed: false`
- `.chezmoiscripts/global/20_ansible_roles.sh: exit status 2`; `PLAY RECAP … failed=1`
- Worked fine on the same machine days earlier; nobody changed the tap

**First seen**: 2026-06 (Mac mini, macOS 26.2, Homebrew 6.0.2)
**Affects**: Homebrew ≥ 6.0 on any OS, any third-party tap this repo uses (`raine/workmux`, `dlvhdr/formulae`)
**Status**: fixed in repo (`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` trust task)

## Symptom

`chezmoi apply` / `chezmoi update` dies in the `devtools` role:

\```
[24] TASK · [devtools : Install developer CLI tools (macOS)]
[ERROR]: Task failed: Module failed: Error: Refusing to load formula raine/workmux/workmux from untrusted tap raine/workmux.
Run `brew trust --formula raine/workmux/workmux` or `brew trust raine/workmux` to trust it.
...
chezmoi: .chezmoiscripts/global/20_ansible_roles.sh: exit status 2
\```

The task taps `raine/workmux` and `dlvhdr/formulae` (via `community.general.homebrew_tap`)
and then `brew install`s `workmux` + `diffnav` from them. The tap succeeds; the
**install** refuses. Even after manually trusting `raine/workmux`, the next run
fails again on `dlvhdr/formulae` — **both** taps are untrusted.

## Root cause

**Homebrew 6.0 added a formula-trust security gate.** `brew install` now refuses
to load formulae from third-party (non-core, non-cask) taps until the tap is
explicitly trusted. `community.general.homebrew_tap` taps the repo but has **no
trust parameter** (the feature is newer than the module), so the formula stays
untrusted and the install fails.

Confirm state with `brew tap-info <tap>` — an untrusted tap shows a literal
`Untrusted` line:

\```
$ brew tap-info raine/workmux
raine/workmux: Installed
Untrusted          # <-- this line is the gate
1 formula
\```

Older Homebrew (< 6.0) has no trust concept at all — `tap-info` never prints
`Untrusted`, so this trap simply cannot occur there.

## Workaround

Trust the whole tap (one-liner, idempotent):

\```bash
brew trust raine/workmux
brew trust dlvhdr/formulae
# or per-formula: brew trust --formula raine/workmux/workmux
\```

Then re-run `chezmoi apply` (or the ansible `devtools` tag).

## Prevention

The `devtools` role now trusts its third-party taps automatically, between the
`homebrew_tap` tasks and the install task. It checks `brew tap-info` for the
`Untrusted` line and only runs `brew trust` when needed (so it no-ops on older
Homebrew and on already-trusted machines):

\```yaml
- name: Check trust state of third-party taps (macOS, Homebrew >= 6.0 formula-trust gate)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew tap-info {{ item }}"
  loop:
    - dlvhdr/formulae
    - raine/workmux
  register: devtools_tap_info
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Trust untrusted third-party taps (macOS)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
    - "'Untrusted' in item.stdout"
  ansible.builtin.command: "brew trust {{ item.item }}"
  loop: "{{ devtools_tap_info.results }}"
  loop_control:
    label: "{{ item.item }}"
  changed_when: true
\```

**Any new third-party tap added to `devtools` (or another role) must be added to
this `loop` too** — a tapped-but-untrusted formula silently blocks the entire
ansible run.

## Related

- `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — the tap + trust + install tasks
- [`docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`](../docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md) — tap/trust note
- Sibling: [`brew-bundle-redownloads-manually-installed-cask`](brew-bundle-redownloads-manually-installed-cask.md)

# macFUSE "Unsupported macOS Version" — `rclone mount` won't mount after a macOS upgrade

**Symptoms** (grep this section):
- macFUSE dialog: **"Unsupported macOS Version — The installed version of macFUSE
  is too old for the operating system. Please upgrade your macFUSE installation
  to one that is compatible with the currently running version of macOS."**
- Fires on boot, on `rclone mount …`, or whenever any FUSE filesystem tries to load
- `rclone mount` fails / hangs even though `rclone mount --help` works and the
  remote is configured correctly
- `brew info --cask macfuse` shows a **newer** version than what's actually on disk

**First seen**: 2026-06 (Mac mini, macOS 26.2, macFUSE 4.10.2 installed)
**Affects**: macOS major upgrades (here macOS 26 "Tahoe") with a macFUSE 4.x kext/system-extension still installed; cask version 5.x required
**Status**: by design (kext version-locked to macOS major); manual upgrade documented — **not** managed by this repo

## Symptom

After upgrading to macOS 26.2, the macFUSE "Unsupported macOS Version" dialog
appears and `rclone mount` silently fails. The trap is that **rclone looks
innocent** — both the Homebrew rclone and the official build have the `mount`
subcommand compiled in (verify: `rclone mount --help` → exits 0), so the binary
is not the problem. macFUSE is the runtime dependency, and it's too old.

The confusing part — `brew` *reports* the right version but it isn't installed:

\```
$ brew info --cask macfuse
==> macfuse (macFUSE): 5.2.0 (auto_updates)      # <-- what the cask points to
Installed
/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/macfuse/4.10.2 (15.4MB)   # <-- what's actually on disk
  Installed on 2025-08-01 ...
\```

`brew upgrade` does **not** fix it: the cask is `auto_updates`, so Homebrew
defers version management to the app — but macFUSE is a system extension that
can't silently self-update; it needs a reinstall + reboot + GUI approval.

## Root cause

macFUSE ships a kernel/system extension that is **version-locked to the macOS
major version**. macFUSE 4.x is not loadable on macOS 26 — macOS 26 needs
macFUSE 5.x. The old extension stays installed across the OS upgrade and macOS
rejects it at load time, hence the dialog. rclone (brew or official) is unaffected;
it just can't get a working FUSE layer to mount onto.

## Workaround

\```bash
brew reinstall --cask macfuse          # pulls the current 5.x pkg
# reboot
# System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ allow the blocked system extension
#   (team "Benjamin Fleischer") ▸ enter password
# reboot again if macOS prompts
rclone mount myremote: ~/mnt/myremote --vfs-cache-mode full --daemon   # now works
\```

## Prevention

- After **any macOS major upgrade**, `brew reinstall --cask macfuse` before
  relying on `rclone mount` / any FUSE filesystem.
- This is **not** automated in this repo: macFUSE needs a reboot + GUI security
  approval, which violates the install-only philosophy (and ansible can't click
  the Privacy & Security toggle). Documented in
  [`docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`](../docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md) and
  [`docs/infra/shared-storage.md`](../docs/infra/shared-storage.md).

### Aside: rclone binary sprawl is harmless here

The same machine had three rclone binaries on `PATH`
(`~/.local/bin/rclone` official, `/opt/homebrew/bin/rclone` brew,
`/usr/local/bin/rclone` a stray root-owned manual install). All support `mount`;
none was the cause. Optional tidy-up: keep one (brew's is fine — modern Homebrew
rclone ≥ 1.73 is built with `cmount`/macFUSE support) and remove the others.

## Summary

**Root-cause findings (the premise was outdated):**
- **`chezmoi apply` failure is not rclone-related.** Homebrew 6.0 added a formula-trust gate; both third-party taps (`raine/workmux`, `dlvhdr/formulae`) were `Untrusted`, so `brew install` refused to load them. The task died on `workmux`; `diffnav` would've been next.
- **Brew rclone *does* support mount now** (`/opt/homebrew/bin/rclone mount --help` → rc=0; modern rclone ≥1.73 is built with `cmount`). No install-method change needed on either OS.
- **The real macOS mount blocker is macFUSE** — yours is 4.10.2, rejected by macOS 26.2 (the "Unsupported macOS Version" dialog). macFUSE isn't repo-managed (needs reboot + GUI approval).

**Changes made:**
1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — new idempotent tap-trust step (checks `brew tap-info` for `Untrusted`, runs `brew trust` only when needed; no-ops on older Homebrew and on already-trusted machines). **This unblocks `chezmoi apply`.**
2. `pitfalls/homebrew-6-refuses-untrusted-tap-formula.md` — new (symptom: the exact "Refusing to load formula … untrusted tap" error).
3. `pitfalls/macfuse-too-old-unsupported-macos-version-rclone-mount.md` — new (symptom: the macFUSE dialog; rclone is *not* the cause; manual `brew reinstall --cask macfuse` + reboot + approval).
4. `pitfalls/README.md` — both indexed (alphabetical).
5. `docs/infra/shared-storage.md` — macOS macFUSE prerequisite note on the rclone-mount section.
6. `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` + `.zh-TW.md` — rclone row annotated.

**Verified:** YAML valid; `brew trust` flipped both taps `Untrusted → Trusted`; previously-failing formulae now load.

**For you to do manually** (per your "document only" choice, to actually get `rclone mount` working on macOS 26): `brew reinstall --cask macfuse` → reboot → approve the system extension in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security. Optional tidy-up: you have 3 rclone binaries on PATH (`~/.local/bin`, brew, and a stray root-owned `/usr/local/bin/rclone`) — keeping brew's alone is fine.

I haven't committed anything. Want me to commit these changes?

fix(devtools): brew trust third-party taps (Homebrew 6 formula-trust gate)

Homebrew 6.0 refuses to load formulae from untrusted third-party taps, so
`brew install workmux`/`diffnav` (raine/workmux, dlvhdr/formulae) failed the
devtools role and aborted `chezmoi apply`. Add an idempotent trust step that
checks `brew tap-info` for "Untrusted" and runs `brew trust` only when needed
(no-ops on older Homebrew and already-trusted hosts).

Also document the rclone-mount-on-macOS reality (the brew binary already
supports mount; the real blocker is an outdated macFUSE kext on macOS 26) via
two new pitfalls + notes in shared-storage and tool-managers. No rclone
install-method change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
